\"security\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2024-11-04\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2025-02-10\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Irene Choi\",\n    \"Priya Natarajan\",\n    \"Jordan Blake\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"retention\",\n    \"data-management\",\n    \"logs\",\n    \"hosted-api\",\n    \"dedicated\",\n    \"private\"\n  ],\n  \"confidentiality\": \"restricted\",\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"confluence://security-and-compliance/audit-logging/audit-log-retention-and-access\",\n    \"confluence://sales-enablement/security-faq/data-retention-and-deletion-faq\"\n  ],\n  \"body\": \"# Purpose\\nThis page defines the default retention and deletion timeframes for customer data and operational logs across Redwood Inference products (Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private).\\n\\n# Definitions (quick)\\n- Customer content: prompts, files, and model outputs (request/response payloads).\\n- Operational logs: API gateway logs, runtime logs, error logs, and request metadata (e.g., request id, status code, latency).\\n- Debug payload logging: optional feature that stores limited request/response payloads for troubleshooting.\\n- Audit logs: security-relevant actions (e.g., login, key creation, RBAC changes).\\n\\n# Default retention windows\\n## Hosted API (Redwood-managed)\\n- Customer content (prompts/outputs): Not stored persistently by default.\\n- Debug payload logging (if explicitly enabled for an org): 7 days retention.\\n- Operational request logs (metadata, not payloads): 14 days retention.\\n- Tracing spans linked to request ids (no payloads): 14 days retention.\\n\\n## Dedicated (Redwood-managed, isolated capacity)\\n- Customer content (prompts/outputs): Not stored persistently by default.\\n- Debug payload logging (if enabled): 7 days retention.\\n- Operational request logs (metadata, not payloads): 14 days retention by default.\\n- Enterprise retention add-on (contracted): Operational request logs can be extended to 30 days (requires Security approval and support runbook change).\\n\\n## Private (VPC / on-prem)\\n- Customer content + operational logs: Retention is customer-configurable because storage is customer-managed.\\n- Private default installer values (if customer does not change settings): 30 days for operational logs in the in-cluster log store.\\n- Redwood control-plane access logs (when Redwood engineers access the private control plane for support): 90 days retention in Redwood systems.\\n\\n# Deletion requests\\n- If a customer submits a deletion request for stored data within Redwood-managed systems (e.g., debug payload logs), Redwood will complete deletion within 30 days of verification of the request.\\n\\n# Notes and guardrails\\n- Debug payload logging must be explicitly enabled and is intended for time-bounded troubleshooting.\\n- Any change to retention windows for Redwood-managed systems requires Security + SRE review and an update to the customer-facing document.content:
{
  "title": "Customer data + logs retention policy (Hosted, Dedicated, Private)",
  "space": "security-and-compliance",
  "author": "Naomi Feldman",
  "owner_team": "security",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2024-11-04",
  "last_updated": "2025-02-10",
  "reviewers": [
    "Irene Choi",
    "Priya Natarajan",
    "Jordan Blake"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "retention",
    "data-management",
    "logs",
    "hosted-api",
    "dedicated",
    "private"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "restricted",
  "related_pages": [
    "confluence://security-and-compliance/audit-logging/audit-log-retention-and-access",
    "confluence://sales-enablement/security-faq/data-retention-and-deletion-faq"
  ],
  "body": "# Purpose\nThis page defines the default retention and deletion timeframes for customer data and operational logs across Redwood Inference products (Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private).\n\n# Definitions (quick)\n- Customer content: prompts, files, and model outputs (request/response payloads).\n- Operational logs: API gateway logs, runtime logs, error logs, and request metadata (e.g., request id, status code, latency).\n- Debug payload logging: optional feature that stores limited request/response payloads for troubleshooting.\n- Audit logs: security-relevant actions (e.g., login, key creation, RBAC changes).\n\n# Default retention windows\n## Hosted API (Redwood-managed)\n- Customer content (prompts/outputs): Not stored persistently by default.\n- Debug payload logging (if explicitly enabled for an org): 7 days retention.\n- Operational request logs (metadata, not payloads): 14 days retention.\n- Tracing spans linked to request ids (no payloads): 14 days retention.\n\n## Dedicated (Redwood-managed, isolated capacity)\n- Customer content (prompts/outputs): Not stored persistently by default.\n- Debug payload logging (if enabled): 7 days retention.\n- Operational request logs (metadata, not payloads): 14 days retention by default.\n- Enterprise retention add-on (contracted): Operational request logs can be extended to 30 days (requires Security approval and support runbook change).\n\n## Private (VPC / on-prem)\n- Customer content + operational logs: Retention is customer-configurable because storage is customer-managed.\n- Private default installer values (if customer does not change settings): 30 days for operational logs in the in-cluster log store.\n- Redwood control-plane access logs (when Redwood engineers access the private control plane for support): 90 days retention in Redwood systems.\n\n# Deletion requests\n- If a customer submits a deletion request for stored data within Redwood-managed systems (e.g., debug payload logs), Redwood will complete deletion within 30 days of verification of the request.\n\n# Notes and guardrails\n- Debug payload logging must be explicitly enabled and is intended for time-bounded troubleshooting.\n- Any change to retention windows for Redwood-managed systems requires Security + SRE review and an update to the customer-facing Security FAQ.",
  "title_field_name": "title",
  "content_field_names": [
    "body"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_e51021765c694a65bd60b3d38b12db6e"
}

    "content": "{\n  \"thread_id\": \"gmail-aditya-20280220-00087\",\n  \"mailbox_owner\": \"aditya_rao\",\n  \"subject\": \"Data disposition & residency \\u2014 Hosted API questionnaire\",\n  \"participants_internal\": [\n    \"Aditya Rao\",\n    \"Neha Kapoor\",\n    \"Marissa Cole\"\n  ],\n  \"participants_external\": [\n    \"Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@glomerate.com>\",\n    \"Glomerate Procurement <procurement@glomerate.com>\"\n  ],\n  \"message_count\": \"4\",\n  \"first_email_at\": \"2028-02-20T09:12:00-08:00\",\n  \"last_email_at\": \"2028-02-22T14:05:00-08:00\",\n  \"thread_type\": \"security_compliance\",\n  \"related_account\": \"Glomerate Inc.\",\n  \"deal_id\": \"DL-3892\",\n  \"region\": \"us\",\n  \"has_attachments\": \"true\",\n  \"attachments\": [\n    \"redwood-data-disposition-statement.pdf\",\n    \"Glomerate-Security-Responses-SectionB.pdf\"\n  ],\n  \"related_links\": [\n    \"https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1xY-example\",\n    \"https://docusign.net/Glomerate-Redwood-SecResponses-12345\",\n    \"https://redwood-secure.example.com/data-disposition\"\n  ],\n  \"messages\": [\n    \"From: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@glomerate.com>\\nTo: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>\\nDate: Mon, 20 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800\\nSubject: Hosted API \\u2014 data residency & disposition questions (Glomerate)\\n\\nHi Aditya,\\n\\nThanks for the quick intro call earlier. To move this through our procurement/security review I need written answers for a short set of questions about Redwood's hosted API handling of customer data. Please provide short, precise answers we can include in our RFP. Key items we need:\\n\\n1) Where is customer content (request/response payloads, logs) stored geographically for the hosted API? Can this be restricted to a single region (US-EAST, EU) for our account?\\n2) Default retention for request/response logs and diagnostic traces; can retention be shortened by contract (e.g., 7 days)?\\n3) Deletion guarantees: when a customer requests deletion, how quickly is data removed from primary storage and from backups/snapshots? What are the SLAs for purge propagation?\\n4) Backups and disaster recovery: are backups encrypted separately? What is the maximum backup retention period?\\n5) Encryption and key management: do you offer customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for hosted API stored data?\\n6) Process for verification/audit: what artifacts can you provide (logs, deletion receipts) to confirm a deletion request was completed?\\n\\nIf you can attach a short statement or diagram that we can attach to our questionnaire, that would be great.\\n\\nLooking to get this back by EOD Thursday (US PST) if possible.\\n\\nThanks,\\nElena Martinez\\nSecurity Operations\\nGlomerate Inc.\\n\\n[Attachment requested: Section B of Glomerate security questionnaire]\\n\",\n    \"From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>\\nTo: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@glomerate.com>\\nCc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>\\nDate: Mon, 20 Feb 2028 11:30:00 -0800\\nSubject: Re: Hosted API \\u2014 data residency & disposition questions (Glomerate)\\n\\nElena,\\n\\nThanks \\u2014 attaching a consolidated statement for your questionnaire and answering inline below. Neha and Marissa are looped in to confirm technical details and add any contractual options.\\n\\nOn Mon, Feb 20, 2028 at 9:12 AM Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@glomerate.com> wrote:\\n> 1) Where is customer content ... Can this be restricted to a single region?\\n\\nAnswer: Customer request/response payloads and associated operational logs for the hosted API are stored in the cloud region selected at account creation (we support US-EAST, US-WEST, EU-WEST, and APAC regions). For enterprise customers we support region-locking so data is kept and processed only within the selected region.\\n\\n> 2) Default retention for logs; can retention be shortened?\\n\\nAnswer: Default retention for request/response logs and diagnostic traces is 30 days. For enterprise contracts we can reduce retention to 7 days or implement a configurable retention policy as part of the account profile.\\n\\n> 3) Deletion guarantees and propagation to backups?\\n\\nAnswer: Deletion requests initiated via the Console or Support ticket remove data from active primary storage within 72 hours. Purge from immutable backups and snapshots is propagated within 14 days; we provide a deletion confirmation once propagation completes. For customers requiring accelerated purges we offer contractual SLAs and additional deletion workflows.\\n\\n> 4) Backups and DR retention?\\n\\nAnswer: Backups are encrypted and retained up to 60 days by default. Longer retention can be negotiated; disaster recovery snapshots are stored in the same region unless cross-region DR is requested and contractually agreed.\\n\\n> 5) Encryption / KMS?\\n\\nAnswer: All data at rest is encrypted (AES-256); in transit uses TLS 1.3. We support both Redwood-managed keys and customer-managed keys via cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS). HSM-backed KMS is available for enterprise plans.\\n\\n> 6) Verification / audit artifacts?\\n\\nAnswer: We provide deletion receipts, per-request audit logs, and exportable activity logs for the retention/deletion events. SOC 2-type evidence and sample deletion receipts are in the attached statement.\\n\\nAttaching: redwood-data-disposition-statement.pdf \\u2014 this is a short, non-engineering summary suitable for RFPs.\\n\\nLet us know if you'd like us to convert these to the specific Glomerate Section B format \\u2014 happy to fill in and return.\\n\\nBest,\\nAditya Rao\\nEnterprise Sales | Redwood Inference\\naditya.rao@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123\\n\\n[Attachment: redwood-data-disposition-statement.pdf (pdf, 12KB)]\\n\",\n    \"From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>\\nTo: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>\\nDate: Tue, 21 Feb 2028 08:46:00 -0800\\nSubject: Re: Hosted API \\u2014 data residency & disposition questions (internal clarification)\\n\\nQuick clarifications / proposed wording tweaks for the statement (technical team sign-off):\\n\\n- Region locking: confirm that metadata and control-plane records (account config, billing) are stored in our control plane (US by default) but request/response payloads and logs are pinned to the customer-selected data region. We'll add a single sentence clarifying control-plane vs data-plane separation.\\n\\n- Retention: 30 days default for request/response logs is correct. For debugging we keep high-fidelity diagnostic traces for up to 90 days but those are strictly access-controlled and only accessible by SRE with JIT approval; we should not surface that to customers unless requested.\\n\\n- Deletion propagation: primary-delete within 72 hours; snapshots/backups propagation target 14 days. Note: immutable backups (for legal/incident hold) may extend beyond 14 days \\u2014 if customer requires true legal hold removal that needs an explicit contract clause.\\n\\n- Backups: encrypted with envelope encryption; separate KMS key per customer is available on enterprise plan.\\n\\n- Audit artifacts: we can provide a deletion receipt that includes deletion ticket id, timestamp of primary purge, and timestamp of backup purge propagation. Include example in the attached PDF.\\n\\nI updated the attached PDF with the wording above and added the redwood-secure link to our internal disposition page for evidence.\\n\\nNeha Kapoor\\nHead of Security, Redwood Inference\\nneha.kapoor@redwood.ai\\n\\n[Internal note: if Glomerate requires sub-7-day backup purge, escalate to Legal for amendment to the Master Services Agreement.]\",\n    \"From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>\\nTo: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@glomerate.com>\\nCc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Glomerate Procurement <procurement@glomerate.com>\\nDate: Wed, 22 Feb 2028 14:05:00 -0800\\nSubject: Re: Hosted API \\u2014 data disposition & residency questions (final responses)\\n\\nElena \\u2014 attaching a Glomerate-ready PDF (Section B) with the final answers (see attachment). Key points we've consolidated below for quick paste into your RFP: \\n\\n\\u2022 Data residency: Customer data (request/response payloads, logs) is stored in the customer-selected region. Region-lock (single-region processing and storage) is supported for enterprise accounts. Control-plane metadata may remain in our control plane.\\n\\n\\u2022 Retention: Default request/response and diagnostic log retention is 30 days. Enterprise retention can be shortened to 7 days or set to a custom policy by contract. High-fidelity traces retained up to 90 days are only accessible to SRE under JIT approvals and will not be included in standard exports.\\n\\n\\u2022 Deletion: We purge primary storage within 72 hours and propagate deletion to backups/snapshots within 14 days. We will provide a deletion confirmation that includes ticket id and timestamps. Accelerated purge SLAs can be included in the contract if needed.\\n\\n\\u2022 Backups & DR: Backups are encrypted, envelope-encryption with per-customer keys available on enterprise plans. Default backup retention is 60 days; cross-region DR is optional and contractual.\\n\\n\\u2022 Encryption & KMS: AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.3 in transit. Redwood-managed keys by default; customer-managed cloud KMS and HSM-backed keys available for enterprise.\\n\\n\\u2022 Audit & verification: We provide deletion receipts, exportable audit logs, and sample artifacts. SOC 2 report excerpts are available under NDA.\\n\\nAttached: Glomerate-Security-Responses-SectionB.pdf (filled-in answers) and the public redwood-data-disposition-statement.pdf.\\n\\nIf that looks good I can return this as a signed statement (DocuSign) and loop Legal for any retention/deletion SLA amendments.\\n\\nBest regards,\\nAditya Rao\\nEnterprise Sales | Redwood Inference\\naditya.rao@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123\\n\\n[Attachments: Glomerate-Security-Responses-SectionB.pdf (pdf, 18KB); redwood-data-disposition-statement.pdf (pdf, 12KB)]\"\n  ],\n  \"title_field_name\": \"subject\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"messages\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_49ad83c4629c4d52a3873ef5c501fa5d\"\n}",

{
  "thread_id": "gmail-aditya-20280220-00087",
  "mailbox_owner": "aditya_rao",
  "subject": "Data disposition & residency — Hosted API questionnaire",
  "participants_internal": [
    "Aditya Rao",
    "Neha Kapoor",
    "Marissa Cole"
  ],
  "participants_external": [
    "Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@glomerate.com>",
    "Glomerate Procurement <procurement@glomerate.com>"
  ],
  "message_count": "4",
  "first_email_at": "2028-02-20T09:12:00-08:00",
  "last_email_at": "2028-02-22T14:05:00-08:00",
  "thread_type": "security_compliance",
  "related_account": "Glomerate Inc.",
  "deal_id": "DL-3892",
  "region": "us",
  "has_attachments": "true",
  "attachments": [
    "redwood-data-disposition-statement.pdf",
    "Glomerate-Security-Responses-SectionB.pdf"
  ],
  "related_links": [
    "https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1xY-example",
    "https://docusign.net/Glomerate-Redwood-SecResponses-12345",
    "https://redwood-secure.example.com/data-disposition"
  ],
  "messages": [
    "From: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@glomerate.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted API — data residency & disposition questions (Glomerate)

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier. To move this through our procurement/security review I need written answers for a short set of questions about Redwood's hosted API handling of customer data. Please provide short, precise answers we can include in our RFP. Key items we need:

1) Where is customer content (request/response payloads, logs) stored geographically for the hosted API? Can this be restricted to a single region (US-EAST, EU) for our account?
2) Default retention for request/response logs and diagnostic traces; can retention be shortened by contract (e.g., 7 days)?
3) Deletion guarantees: when a customer requests deletion, how quickly is data removed from primary storage and from backups/snapshots? What are the SLAs for purge propagation?
4) Backups and disaster recovery: are backups encrypted separately? What is the maximum backup retention period?
5) Encryption and key management: do you offer customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for hosted API stored data?
6) Process for verification/audit: what artifacts can you provide (logs, deletion receipts) to confirm a deletion request was completed?

If you can attach a short statement or diagram that we can attach to our questionnaire, that would be great.

Looking to get this back by EOD Thursday (US PST) if possible.

Thanks,
Elena Martinez
Security Operations
Glomerate Inc.

[Attachment requested: Section B of Glomerate security questionnaire]
",
    "From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@glomerate.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Feb 2028 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API — data residency & disposition questions (Glomerate)

Elena,

Thanks — attaching a consolidated statement for your questionnaire and answering inline below. Neha and Marissa are looped in to confirm technical details and add any contractual options.

On Mon, Feb 20, 2028 at 9:12 AM Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@glomerate.com> wrote:
> 1) Where is customer content ... Can this be restricted to a single region?

Answer: Customer request/response payloads and associated operational logs for the hosted API are stored in the cloud region selected at account creation (we support US-EAST, US-WEST, EU-WEST, and APAC regions). For enterprise customers we support region-locking so data is kept and processed only within the selected region.

> 2) Default retention for logs; can retention be shortened?

Answer: Default retention for request/response logs and diagnostic traces is 30 days. For enterprise contracts we can reduce retention to 7 days or implement a configurable retention policy as part of the account profile.

> 3) Deletion guarantees and propagation to backups?

Answer: Deletion requests initiated via the Console or Support ticket remove data from active primary storage within 72 hours. Purge from immutable backups and snapshots is propagated within 14 days; we provide a deletion confirmation once propagation completes. For customers requiring accelerated purges we offer contractual SLAs and additional deletion workflows.

> 4) Backups and DR retention?

Answer: Backups are encrypted and retained up to 60 days by default. Longer retention can be negotiated; disaster recovery snapshots are stored in the same region unless cross-region DR is requested and contractually agreed.

> 5) Encryption / KMS?

Answer: All data at rest is encrypted (AES-256); in transit uses TLS 1.3. We support both Redwood-managed keys and customer-managed keys via cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS). HSM-backed KMS is available for enterprise plans.

> 6) Verification / audit artifacts?

Answer: We provide deletion receipts, per-request audit logs, and exportable activity logs for the retention/deletion events. SOC 2-type evidence and sample deletion receipts are in the attached statement.

Attaching: redwood-data-disposition-statement.pdf — this is a short, non-engineering summary suitable for RFPs.

Let us know if you'd like us to convert these to the specific Glomerate Section B format — happy to fill in and return.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

[Attachment: redwood-data-disposition-statement.pdf (pdf, 12KB)]
",
    "From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Feb 2028 08:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API — data residency & disposition questions (internal clarification)

Quick clarifications / proposed wording tweaks for the statement (technical team sign-off):

- Region locking: confirm that metadata and control-plane records (account config, billing) are stored in our control plane (US by default) but request/response payloads and logs are pinned to the customer-selected data region. We'll add a single sentence clarifying control-plane vs data-plane separation.

- Retention: 30 days default for request/response logs is correct. For debugging we keep high-fidelity diagnostic traces for up to 90 days but those are strictly access-controlled and only accessible by SRE with JIT approval; we should not surface that to customers unless requested.

- Deletion propagation: primary-delete within 72 hours; snapshots/backups propagation target 14 days. Note: immutable backups (for legal/incident hold) may extend beyond 14 days — if customer requires true legal hold removal that needs an explicit contract clause.

- Backups: encrypted with envelope encryption; separate KMS key per customer is available on enterprise plan.

- Audit artifacts: we can provide a deletion receipt that includes deletion ticket id, timestamp of primary purge, and timestamp of backup purge propagation. Include example in the attached PDF.

I updated the attached PDF with the wording above and added the redwood-secure link to our internal disposition page for evidence.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

[Internal note: if Glomerate requires sub-7-day backup purge, escalate to Legal for amendment to the Master Services Agreement.]",
    "From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Martinez <elena.martinez@glomerate.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Glomerate Procurement <procurement@glomerate.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Feb 2028 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API — data disposition & residency questions (final responses)

Elena — attaching a Glomerate-ready PDF (Section B) with the final answers (see attachment). Key points we've consolidated below for quick paste into your RFP: 

• Data residency: Customer data (request/response payloads, logs) is stored in the customer-selected region. Region-lock (single-region processing and storage) is supported for enterprise accounts. Control-plane metadata may remain in our control plane.

• Retention: Default request/response and diagnostic log retention is 30 days. Enterprise retention can be shortened to 7 days or set to a custom policy by contract. High-fidelity traces retained up to 90 days are only accessible to SRE under JIT approvals and will not be included in standard exports.

• Deletion: We purge primary storage within 72 hours and propagate deletion to backups/snapshots within 14 days. We will provide a deletion confirmation that includes ticket id and timestamps. Accelerated purge SLAs can be included in the contract if needed.

• Backups & DR: Backups are encrypted, envelope-encryption with per-customer keys available on enterprise plans. Default backup retention is 60 days; cross-region DR is optional and contractual.

• Encryption & KMS: AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.3 in transit. Redwood-managed keys by default; customer-managed cloud KMS and HSM-backed keys available for enterprise.

• Audit & verification: We provide deletion receipts, exportable audit logs, and sample artifacts. SOC 2 report excerpts are available under NDA.

Attached: Glomerate-Security-Responses-SectionB.pdf (filled-in answers) and the public redwood-data-disposition-statement.pdf.

If that looks good I can return this as a signed statement (DocuSign) and loop Legal for any retention/deletion SLA amendments.

Best regards,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

[Attachments: Glomerate-Security-Responses-SectionB.pdf (pdf, 18KB); redwood-data-disposition-statement.pdf (pdf, 12KB)]"

    "title": "Residency & evidence-gathering discovery - Silverline Capital",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/fireflies",
    "content": "{\n  \"meeting_id\": \"ff-20260605-3749\",\n  \"recorded_at\": \"2026-06-05T15:00:00-07:00\",\n  \"duration_minutes\": \"55\",\n  \"call_type\": \"discovery\",\n  \"title\": \"Residency & evidence-gathering discovery - Silverline Capital\",\n  \"redwood_owner\": \"Adam Reed\",\n  \"redwood_attendees\": [\n    \"Adam Reed (AE)\",\n    \"Priya Nair (SE)\",\n    \"Lena Ortiz (CSM)\"\n  ],\n  \"customer_company\": \"Silverline Capital\",\n  \"customer_attendees\": [\n    \"Marta Alvarez (Head of Data Privacy)\",\n    \"Samir Patel (Lead Platform Engineer)\",\n    \"Janelle Chu (Compliance Manager)\",\n    \"Michael O'Neal (CTO)\"\n  ],\n  \"competitors_mentioned\": [\n    \"Anthropic\",\n    \"OpenAI\",\n    \"Internal bare-metal infra\"\n  ],\n  \"crm_deal_id\": \"SFDC-0047821\",\n  \"transcription_quality\": \"medium\",\n  \"topics\": [\n    \"Data residency requirements\",\n    \"Audit logs & retention\",\n    \"Encryption/KMS & HSM\",\n    \"Private vs Hosted vs Dedicated\",\n    \"DSAR/deletion workflows\",\n    \"SAML/SSO & RBAC\"\n  ],\n  \"summary\": \"Initial discovery to map Silverline's regulatory evidence requirements and constraints for deploying LLM inference. Focus on log retention limits, redaction/PII controls, region locking, and evidence packaging for auditors.\",\n  \"action_items\": [\n    \"Adam Reed | Send compliance pack (SOC2 + infra diagrams) | Due: 2026-06-09\",\n    \"Priya Nair | Run a quick latency/cost estimate for Dedicated in eu-west-1 vs hosted via controlled region | Due: 2026-06-12\",\n    \"Marta Alvarez | Share the list of regulatory auditors and required artifact formats (CSV/JSON/PDF) | Due: 2026-06-10\",\n    \"Samir Patel | Provide network topology and firewall rules for VPC peering checklist | Due: 2026-06-11\"\n  ],\n  \"next_steps\": [\n    \"Redwood to share compliance deck and data handling playbook\",\n    \"Schedule technical deep dive with infra team (Priya + Samir) next week\",\n    \"Customer to confirm which environments need region-locking (prod vs staging)\"\n  ],\n  \"transcript\": \"Meeting header\\nDate: 2026-06-05\\nTime: 15:00 PT (PDT)\\nDuration: 55 min\\nAttendees: Adam Reed (Redwood AE); Priya Nair (Redwood SE); Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Marta Alvarez (Silverline - Head of Data Privacy); Samir Patel (Silverline - Lead Platform Eng); Janelle Chu (Silverline - Compliance); Michael O'Neal (Silverline CTO)\\nLinks shared: redwood_compliance_deck.pdf, preliminary-benchmark.xlsx, private-deploy-guide.md\\n\\nSummary:\\n15:00 - quick intros and goals - map compliance evidence + constraints, decide host/dedicated/private feasibility\\n\\nTopics:\\n- Primary regs: GDPR (EUD), UK-DPA, FINRA-ish reporting, and potential HIPAA scoping for a new health-vertical product\\n- Logging: what we store, retention windows, redaction (PII), access controls, encryption at rest/in transit\\n- Deployment modes: hosted with region locking, Dedicated reserved capacity, Private VPC/on-prem\\n- Evidence & audit-ready exports: format, chain-of-custody, who signs off\\n\\nTranscript:\\n[00:00] Adam Reed: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick round-robin \\u2014 I'm Adam, AE on Redwood, with Priya our SE and Lena from customer success. Marta, do you want to lead with the why for today's chat?\\n[00:18] Marta Alvarez: Yeah hi \\u2014 thanks. So Silverline's preparing to spin up an LLM-powered compliance-assist feature for our institutional clients, and our audit team wants to know: can we prove where data lived, how logs were retained, and show evidence to FINRA-style auditors. We're also juggling GDPR DSARs and a potential HIPAA interplay. So trying to map options: hosted, dedicated, or fully private.\\n[00:43] Priya Nair: Great, that's exactly the kind of scope we help model. First clarifying question \\u2014 do you have any regulatory constraints that require on-prem or is cloud region locking acceptable? In other words, is the barrier data residency or cert-level isolation?\\n[01:06] Samir Patel: Right now cloud is fine, but the legal team insists that production PII must never leave eu-west for EU customers, and US financial workloads need logs retained for seven years per our retention policy. Also, some auditors want the full raw request/response logs, others only hashed payloads \\u2014 depends on the case.\\n[01:31] Janelle Chu: And to add, for certain clients we need attestations that keys are customer-managed via KMS/HSM so we can show key custody separation.\\n[01:42] Adam Reed: Understood. High level \\u2014 Redwood hosted can be region-locked so your tenant is pinned to eu-west-1 and us-east-1, but Hosted does keep some control-plane telemetry in our backend; we do offer options to limit what is persisted. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools in your tenancy with stricter separation and more fine-grained log controls, and Private gives you a customer-managed control plane.\\n[02:15] Michael O'Neal: When you say \\\"control-plane telemetry\\\" \\u2014 can you give examples? Are we talking metrics and anonymized traces or request payloads?\\n[02:27] Priya Nair: Mostly metrics, orchestration traces, and runtime health; request and full prompt data are considered customer data and by default are stored per your retention settings. That said, we can configure no-persist for content on Dedicated/Private but that has tradeoffs \\u2014 e.g., you lose KV cache warm start benefits and some batching optimizations which can affect latency/cost.\\n[03:00] Marta Alvarez: \\\"No-persist\\\" sounds promising but auditors want chain-of-custody \\u2014 how do you prove logs weren't modified? Is there an immutable export or signed evidence?\\n[03:14] Priya Nair: We have an audit export that zips logs with a manifest and a signing hash. For Dedicated/Private, the manifests can be generated in-customer infra and signed with your KMS key, or we can provide a Redwood-signed artifact for hosted. There's occasional confusion: our signed exports are not the same as H S M-signed hardware attestation but they do include a tamper-evident hash chain.\\n[03:46] Samir Patel: We're going to need the option to redact PII before logs are exported \\u2014 can Redwood do field-level redaction in the runtime? Like strip or mask account numbers, SSNs, etc.\\n[04:00] Priya Nair: Yes, we support configurable redaction rules pre-export, plus anonymization hooks that run in the serving path. One caveat \\u2014 pre-export redaction affects your ability to replay the exact raw prompt if an auditor requests it; we often recommend maintaining a hashed token mapping for reproducibility while never storing raw PII.\\n[04:26] Janelle Chu: For GDPR DSARs, we need the ability to locate all data tied to an identifier and purge it. Does Redwood support selective deletion across caches and logs?\\n[04:39] Adam Reed: We support DSAR workflows \\u2014 deletion across persistent logs and object stores, and a KV invalidation endpoint to purge cached keys. On Hosted we can perform deletions for you if you authorise but we can also provide API endpoints so you can automate it from your side on Dedicated/Private.\\n[05:00] Speaker 3: Uh \\u2014 quick question, what's the retention cap on hosted? I thought there was a default 30 days?\\n[05:10] Adam Reed: Default is 30 days for ephemeral logs on Hosted, but we can extend retention on a contract basis to meet regulatory needs \\u2014 including multi-year retention for financials. That said, storing multi-year raw prompts increases costs and we often recommend summarization/payload hashing for long-term storage.\\n[05:34] Marta Alvarez: Can you describe DR and region-failover? Auditors expect continuity plans and proof data never left jurisdiction even during failover.\\n[05:46] Priya Nair: For region-failover we do cross-region replication only if you opt in. There is an explicit 'region-lock' feature \\u2014 if enabled, it prevents automatic failover out of region and requires manual approval. That's often used by customers with strict residency requirements.\\n[06:10] Samir Patel: Network: if we go Dedicated or Private, what's the common pattern for VPC peering or private link? Are you using S3 endpoints for logs, or do logs pass back to Redwood first?\\n[06:25] Priya Nair: Dedicated and Private typically keep all traffic in your VPC; logs can be written to customer S3 buckets via VPC endpoints so Redwood doesn't see raw logs. For Hosted, logs usually land in Redwood-managed storage unless you elect a cross-account delivery. We'll provide a network checklist.\\n[06:45] Adam Reed: I'll attach a VPC checklist. Also note for Private on-prem installs, the audit artifacts are entirely customer-managed.\\n[06:55] Michael O'Neal: What about certs and compliance evidence? Our auditors will ask for SOC2 reports, pen test results, and software bill-of-materials.\\n[07:06] Adam Reed: We can share our SOC 2 Type II report and pen test summaries. SBOMs \\u2014 we provide high-level SBOMs for runtime components; detailed SBOMs are available under NDA for Private customers.\\n[07:24] Marta Alvarez: For HIPAA \\u2014 if we expand to that health product \\u2014 we'd need BAA. Do you offer BAAs?\\n[07:32] Adam Reed: Yes, BAAs are available for Dedicated and Private customers; Hosted can be covered depending on data flows, but Dedicated/Private is the usual route for PHI workloads.\\n[07:47] Janelle Chu: A few nitty gritty items auditors ask: time synch and signed logs for event correlation, RBAC audit trail \\u2014 can you map tokens to users and store who triggered what?\\n[07:59] Priya Nair: We emit correlated audit events with ISO timestamps and a unique request id. For RBAC we integrate with SSO (SAML/OIDC) and produce admin action logs. There is a small mismatch sometimes around naming: our admin audit logs are separate from per-request logs, auditors sometimes want a single bundle; we can produce a combined export.\\n[08:30] Samir Patel: On keys \\u2014 you said KMS integration, but can we bring our own HSM? We want customer-held master keys.\\n[08:40] Priya Nair: For Dedicated we support CMEK via your cloud KMS, and Private on-prem can integrate with HSMs. For Hosted, we offer customer-managed keys via cross-account KMS setup in some cases.\\n[08:56] Marta Alvarez: Ok, about evidence forms \\u2014 auditors want CSV with user-id, timestamp, request-id, redacted-prompt, model-version, response-hash. Is that output standard?\\n[09:08] Adam Reed: We can deliver that as a default export format. Some clients request JSON lines for ingest into their SIEM. We can do both.\\n[09:20] Speaker 2: There's also concern about model provenance \\u2014 auditors ask which model version and quantization were used.\\n[09:28] Priya Nair: We log model metadata (version, quantization, runtime flags) with each request so you can show exact configuration. Note mislabeling can happen if models are rolled \\u2014 we recommend pinning model versions for regulated workloads.\\n[09:48] Marta Alvarez: Good. On the subject of redaction \\u2014 can the redaction rules be reviewed by our compliance team? They want to ensure the regexes are strict enough.\\n[09:58] Priya Nair: Absolutely. We can provide a rule preview tool and a staging export so your team can validate before enabling in prod.\\n[10:10] Samir Patel: If we wanted zero-retention for certain clients but still provide auditors with evidence, is there a recommended pattern?\\n[10:20] Priya Nair: Common pattern: keep hashed mappings and signed manifests; optionally keep minimal metadata required for auditing (timestamps, model-version, request-id) while redacting content. For deeper audits, customers sometimes perform in-scope reproduction runs in a secure environment with consented replays.\\n[10:42] Janelle Chu: About access \\u2014 we need log access controls and a separation of duties for who can pull exports. Do you support role-tiered access?\\n[10:54] Adam Reed: Yes, RBAC is supported with roles for auditors, ops, and developers. We also support time-limited export tokens for auditors.\\n[11:06] Marta Alvarez: One more: chain-of-custody proof \\u2014 you mentioned signing with KMS. Is the signing performed within the customer's KMS so Redwood never sees the signing key?\\n[11:18] Priya Nair: For Dedicated/Private yes \\u2014 we can have the manifest signed by your KMS, Redwood only provides the unsigned artifact. For Hosted, we offer Redwood-signed artifacts or a cross-account KMS flow.\\n[11:33] Samir Patel: We might need attestations from a third-party to satisfy risk. Do customers ever ask Redwood for a sub-processor list and contracts?\\n[11:43] Adam Reed: Yes, we maintain a sub-processor list and can share contracts under NDA.\\n[11:50] Michael O'Neal: About live incident response \\u2014 if there's a suspected leak, what's the escalation path and how do we get forensic artifacts quickly?\\n[11:59] Priya Nair: We have a designated incident response flow; we'll provide a runbook. For Dedicated/Private customers, we can grant expedited access to raw logs or snapshots; for Hosted it's via support with SLA tiers.\\n[12:20] Marta Alvarez: Great. Could you walk us through the difference between Dedicated and Private in terms of audit evidence ownership once \\u2014 like bullet points.\\n[12:33] Priya Nair: Sure: Dedicated = Redwood-managed control plane but single-tenant compute and stronger separation; you can use customer KMS and private S3 buckets. Evidence can be generated in your account. Private = full customer control plane and infra, everything is in your environment, we package the software and you run it \\u2014 most control for auditors.\\n[13:05] Speaker 1: Any cost delta implications for long-term retention and signing?\\n[13:12] Adam Reed: Retention cost scales with log volume.   "meeting_id": "ff-20260605-3749",

  "call_type": "discovery",
  "title": "Residency & evidence-gathering discovery - Silverline Capital",
  "redwood_owner": "Adam Reed",
  "redwood_attendees": [
    "Adam Reed (AE)",
    "Priya Nair (SE)",
    "Lena Ortiz (CSM)"
  ],
  "customer_company": "Silverline Capital",
  "customer_attendees": [
    "Marta Alvarez (Head of Data Privacy)",
    "Samir Patel (Lead Platform Engineer)",
    "Janelle Chu (Compliance Manager)",
    "Michael O'Neal (CTO)"
  ],

  "crm_deal_id": "SFDC-0047821",

    "Data residency requirements",
    "Audit logs & retention",
    "Encryption/KMS & HSM",
    "Private vs Hosted vs Dedicated",
    "DSAR/deletion workflows",
    "SAML/SSO & RBAC"
  ],
  "summary": "Initial discovery to map Silverline's regulatory evidence requirements and constraints for deploying LLM inference. Focus on log retention limits, redaction/PII controls, region locking, and evidence packaging for auditors.",
  "action_items": [
    "Adam Reed | Send compliance pack (SOC2 + infra diagrams) | Due: 2026-06-09",
    "Priya Nair | Run a quick latency/cost estimate for Dedicated in eu-west-1 vs hosted via controlled region | Due: 2026-06-12",
    "Marta Alvarez | Share the list of regulatory auditors and required artifact formats (CSV/JSON/PDF) | Due: 2026-06-10",
    "Samir Patel | Provide network topology and firewall rules for VPC peering checklist | Due: 2026-06-11"
  ],
  "next_steps": [
    "Redwood to share compliance deck and data handling playbook",
    "Schedule technical deep dive with infra team (Priya + Samir) next week",
    "Customer to confirm which environments need region-locking (prod vs staging)"
  ],
  "transcript": "Meeting header
Date: 2026-06-05
Time: 15:00 PT (PDT)
Duration: 55 min
Attendees: Adam Reed (Redwood AE); Priya Nair (Redwood SE); Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Marta Alvarez (Silverline - Head of Data Privacy); Samir Patel (Silverline - Lead Platform Eng); Janelle Chu (Silverline - Compliance); Michael O'Neal (Silverline CTO)
Links shared: redwood_compliance_deck.pdf, preliminary-benchmark.xlsx, private-deploy-guide.md

Summary:
15:00 - quick intros and goals - map compliance evidence + constraints, decide host/dedicated/private feasibility

Topics:
- Primary regs: GDPR (EUD), UK-DPA, FINRA-ish reporting, and potential HIPAA scoping for a new health-vertical product
- Logging: what we store, retention windows, redaction (PII), access controls, encryption at rest/in transit
- Deployment modes: hosted with region locking, Dedicated reserved capacity, Private VPC/on-prem
- Evidence & audit-ready exports: format, chain-of-custody, who signs off

Transcript:
[00:00] Adam Reed: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick round-robin — I'm Adam, AE on Redwood, with Priya our SE and Lena from customer success. Marta, do you want to lead with the why for today's chat?
[00:18] Marta Alvarez: Yeah hi — thanks. So Silverline's preparing to spin up an LLM-powered compliance-assist feature for our institutional clients, and our audit team wants to know: can we prove where data lived, how logs were retained, and show evidence to FINRA-style auditors. We're also juggling GDPR DSARs and a potential HIPAA interplay. So trying to map options: hosted, dedicated, or fully private.
[00:43] Priya Nair: Great, that's exactly the kind of scope we help model. First clarifying question — do you have any regulatory constraints that require on-prem or is cloud region locking acceptable? In other words, is the barrier data residency or cert-level isolation?
[01:06] Samir Patel: Right now cloud is fine, but the legal team insists that production PII must never leave eu-west for EU customers, and US financial workloads need logs retained for seven years per our retention policy. Also, some auditors want the full raw request/response logs, others only hashed payloads — depends on the case.
[01:31] Janelle Chu: And to add, for certain clients we need attestations that keys are customer-managed via KMS/HSM so we can show key custody separation.
[01:42] Adam Reed: Understood. High level — Redwood hosted can be region-locked so your tenant is pinned to eu-west-1 and us-east-1, but Hosted does keep some control-plane telemetry in our backend; we do offer options to limit what is persisted. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools in your tenancy with stricter separation and more fine-grained log controls, and Private gives you a customer-managed control plane.
[02:15] Michael O'Neal: When you say "control-plane telemetry" — can you give examples? Are we talking metrics and anonymized traces or request payloads?
[02:27] Priya Nair: Mostly metrics, orchestration traces, and runtime health; request and full prompt data are considered customer data and by default are stored per your retention settings. That said, we can configure no-persist for content on Dedicated/Private but that has tradeoffs — e.g., you lose KV cache warm start benefits and some batching optimizations which can affect latency/cost.
[03:00] Marta Alvarez: "No-persist" sounds promising but auditors want chain-of-custody — how do you prove logs weren't modified? Is there an immutable export or signed evidence?
[03:14] Priya Nair: We have an audit export that zips logs with a manifest and a signing hash. For Dedicated/Private, the manifests can be generated in-customer infra and signed with your KMS key, or we can provide a Redwood-signed artifact for hosted. There's occasional confusion: our signed exports are not the same as H S M-signed hardware attestation but they do include a tamper-evident hash chain.
[03:46] Samir Patel: We're going to need the option to redact PII before logs are exported — can Redwood do field-level redaction in the runtime? Like strip or mask account numbers, SSNs, etc.
[04:00] Priya Nair: Yes, we support configurable redaction rules pre-export, plus anonymization hooks that run in the serving path. One caveat — pre-export redaction affects your ability to replay the exact raw prompt if an auditor requests it; we often recommend maintaining a hashed token mapping for reproducibility while never storing raw PII.
[04:26] Janelle Chu: For GDPR DSARs, we need the ability to locate all data tied to an identifier and purge it. Does Redwood support selective deletion across caches and logs?
[04:39] Adam Reed: We support DSAR workflows — deletion across persistent logs and object stores, and a KV invalidation endpoint to purge cached keys. On Hosted we can perform deletions for you if you authorise but we can also provide API endpoints so you can automate it from your side on Dedicated/Private.
[05:00] Speaker 3: Uh — quick question, what's the retention cap on hosted? I thought there was a default 30 days?
[05:10] Adam Reed: Default is 30 days for ephemeral logs on Hosted, but we can extend retention on a contract basis to meet regulatory needs — including multi-year retention for financials. That said, storing multi-year raw prompts increases costs and we often recommend summarization/payload hashing for long-term storage.
[05:34] Marta Alvarez: Can you describe DR and region-failover? Auditors expect continuity plans and proof data never left jurisdiction even during failover.
[05:46] Priya Nair: For region-failover we do cross-region replication only if you opt in. There is an explicit 'region-lock' feature — if enabled, it prevents automatic failover out of region and requires manual approval. That's often used by customers with strict residency requirements.
[06:10] Samir Patel: Network: if we go Dedicated or Private, what's the common pattern for VPC peering or private link? Are you using S3 endpoints for logs, or do logs pass back to Redwood first?
[06:25] Priya Nair: Dedicated and Private typically keep all traffic in your VPC; logs can be written to customer S3 buckets via VPC endpoints so Redwood doesn't see raw logs. For Hosted, logs usually land in Redwood-managed storage unless you elect a cross-account delivery. We'll provide a network checklist.
[06:45] Adam Reed: I'll attach a VPC checklist. Also note for Private on-prem installs, the audit artifacts are entirely customer-managed.
[06:55] Michael O'Neal: What about certs and compliance evidence? Our auditors will ask for SOC2 reports, pen test results, and software bill-of-materials.
[07:06] Adam Reed: We can share our SOC 2 Type II report and pen test summaries. SBOMs — we provide high-level SBOMs for runtime components; detailed SBOMs are available under NDA for Private customers.
[07:24] Marta Alvarez: For HIPAA — if we expand to that health product — we'd need BAA. Do you offer BAAs?
[07:32] Adam Reed: Yes, BAAs are available for Dedicated and Private customers; Hosted can be covered depending on data flows, but Dedicated/Private is the usual route for PHI workloads.
[07:47] Janelle Chu: A few nitty gritty items auditors ask: time synch and signed logs for event correlation, RBAC audit trail — can you map tokens to users and store who triggered what?
[07:59] Priya Nair: We emit correlated audit events with ISO timestamps and a unique request id. For RBAC we integrate with SSO (SAML/OIDC) and produce admin action logs. There is a small mismatch sometimes around naming: our admin audit logs are separate from per-request logs, auditors sometimes want a single bundle; we can produce a combined export.
[08:30] Samir Patel: On keys — you said KMS integration, but can we bring our own HSM? We want customer-held master keys.
[08:40] Priya Nair: For Dedicated we support CMEK via your cloud KMS, and Private on-prem can integrate with HSMs. For Hosted, we offer customer-managed keys via cross-account KMS setup in some cases.
[08:56] Marta Alvarez: Ok, about evidence forms — auditors want CSV with user-id, timestamp, request-id, redacted-prompt, model-version, response-hash. Is that output standard?
[09:08] Adam Reed: We can deliver that as a default export format. Some clients request JSON lines for ingest into their SIEM. We can do both.
[09:20] Speaker 2: There's also concern about model provenance — auditors ask which model version and quantization were used.
[09:28] Priya Nair: We log model metadata (version, quantization, runtime flags) with each request so you can show exact configuration. Note mislabeling can happen if models are rolled — we recommend pinning model versions for regulated workloads.
[09:48] Marta Alvarez: Good. On the subject of redaction — can the redaction rules be reviewed by our compliance team? They want to ensure the regexes are strict enough.
[09:58] Priya Nair: Absolutely. We can provide a rule preview tool and a staging export so your team can validate before enabling in prod.
[10:10] Samir Patel: If we wanted zero-retention for certain clients but still provide auditors with evidence, is there a recommended pattern?
[10:20] Priya Nair: Common pattern: keep hashed mappings and signed manifests; optionally keep minimal metadata required for auditing (timestamps, model-version, request-id) while redacting content. For deeper audits, customers sometimes perform in-scope reproduction runs in a secure environment with consented replays.
[10:42] Janelle Chu: About access — we need log access controls and a separation of duties for who can pull exports. Do you support role-tiered access?
[10:54] Adam Reed: Yes, RBAC is supported with roles for auditors, ops, and developers. We also support time-limited export tokens for auditors.
[11:06] Marta Alvarez: One more: chain-of-custody proof — you mentioned signing with KMS. Is the signing performed within the customer's KMS so Redwood never sees the signing key?
[11:18] Priya Nair: For Dedicated/Private yes — we can have the manifest signed by your KMS, Redwood only provides the unsigned artifact. For Hosted, we offer Redwood-signed artifacts or a cross-account KMS flow.
[11:33] Samir Patel: We might need attestations from a third-party to satisfy risk. Do customers ever ask Redwood for a sub-processor list and contracts?
[11:43] Adam Reed: Yes, we maintain a sub-processor list and can share contracts under NDA.
[11:50] Michael O'Neal: About live incident response — if there's a suspected leak, what's the escalation path and how do we get forensic artifacts quickly?
[11:59] Priya Nair: We have a designated incident response flow; we'll provide a runbook. For Dedicated/Private customers, we can grant expedited access to raw logs or snapshots; for Hosted it's via support with SLA tiers.
[12:20] Marta Alvarez: Great. Could you walk us through the difference between Dedicated and Private in terms of audit evidence ownership once — like bullet points.
[12:33] Priya Nair: Sure: Dedicated = Redwood-managed control plane but single-tenant compute and stronger separation; you can use customer KMS and private S3 buckets. Evidence can be generated in your account. Private = full customer control plane and infra, everything is in your environment, we package the software and you run it — most control for auditors.
[13:05] Speaker 1: Any cost delta implications for long-term retention and signing?
[13:12] Adam Reed: Retention cost scales with log volume. Signing itself is minimal cost but managing long-term storage (S3 Glacier/IA) will be the main contributor. We'll include cost scenarios in the estimate.
[13:28] Marta Alvarez: For the next call, our auditors want a sample exported artifact. Can Redwood produce a redacted sample export that mimics the real thing?
[13:38] Adam Reed: Yes, we'll produce a sample export with pii redacted and include the manifest/hash chain.
[13:45] Samir Patel: Also we'd like a technical deep dive focused on network setup and latency impact for dedicated vs hosted — Priya, can you lead that?
[13:53] Priya Nair: Yep, happy to. I'll propose times.
[14:00] Lena Ortiz: I'll coordinate calendar invites and share the SOC2 + pen test deck after the call.
[14:06] Marta Alvarez: Thanks — helpful. Quick clarifying Q: can Hosted support customer-managed KMS via cross-account key rotation? We have rotating keys and need to ensure past artifacts verify under historical keys.
[14:20] Priya Nair: We can support key rotation and maintain signed manifests with versioned keys. For full verification under historical keys, Dedicated/Private is simpler but Hosted can be configured.
[14:36] Speaker 4: Sorry interrupt — do you have example DSAR API calls?
[14:42] Adam Reed: Yes, we'll include API examples in the follow-up playbook.
[14:48] Marta Alvarez: Any other blockers from our side? I think we need the sample artifact, SOC2, and the network checklist.
[14:56] Adam Reed: Yup. We'll pack those up.
[15:00] Adam Reed: Alright, recap: send compliance pack + sample artifact, schedule tech deep dive, get topology from Samir, Marta to share auditor format. Anything else?
[15:12] Janelle Chu: No that's it, thanks.
[15:15] Michael O'Neal: Thanks all.
[15:18] Adam Reed: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up. End call.

Note: transcription includes occasional mis-hearings (e.g., KV cache noted as KV 'cash' in one segment), some speaker labels auto-assigned by the recorder.

# Hosted API retention and deletion rule

Status: Support-facing interim rule (v1)
Owner: Platform & Console
Scope: Redwood-managed Hosted API

## What Support may state

- Customer content (prompts and outputs) is not stored persistently by default.
- Debug payload logging is off unless explicitly enabled for an organization. When enabled, its default retention is 7 days.
- Operational request logs contain metadata rather than payloads and have a default retention of 14 days.
- Tracing spans linked to request IDs contain no payloads and have a default retention of 14 days.
- For stored data in Redwood-managed systems, Redwood completes a verified deletion request within 30 days.
- Changes to Redwood-managed retention require Security and SRE review and an update to the customer-facing Security FAQ.

These are product defaults, not substitutes for a customer's executed contract or an approved exception.

## What Support must not promise yet

The reviewed published policy does not establish:

- a backup or snapshot purge deadline;
- a tenant-termination-specific purge deadline;
- a data-residency or single-region guarantee;
- whether backups remain in-region or replicate cross-region;
- a standard deletion certificate, receipt, or audit-evidence package;
- legal-hold exceptions or treatment of billing/control-plane metadata;
- customer-configurable Hosted API retention beyond an approved, documented exception.

Sales calls and questionnaire emails contain materially different figures (including 30-day payload/log retention, 72-hour primary deletion, 14- to 90-day backup purge, and region-locking statements). Do not repeat those figures as general policy until Security/SRE and Legal validate them against current production behavior and contract templates.

## Validation before answering a customer

1. Confirm the customer's deployment is Hosted API and identify whether debug payload logging is enabled.
2. Check the executed order form, DPA, and approved retention/residency addenda for customer-specific terms.
3. Escalate backup purge, termination, residency, cross-region, legal-hold, and evidence-package questions to Security/SRE and Legal.
4. For deletion, verify the request and track completion through the support case; do not invent a backup-completion date or certificate commitment.
5. If approved facts change, revise this canonical path and replace its semantic memory rather than publishing parallel guidance.

## Evidence

Authoritative baseline:

- [Customer data + logs retention policy (Hosted, Dedicated, Private)](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/customer-data-and-logs-retention-policy.json) — document `dsid_e51021765c694a65bd60b3d38b12db6e` (published Security policy).

              "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Hosted API retention and deletion rule\nSource: Platform & Console\nPath: /knowledge/policies/hosted-api-retention.md\nWorkspace: task/ethan-park/retention-rule-v1-v3\n\n# Hosted API retention and deletion rule\n\nStatus: Support-facing interim rule (v1)\nOwner: Platform & Console\nScope: Redwood-managed Hosted API\n\n## What Support may state\n\n- Customer content (prompts and outputs) is not stored persistently by default.\n- Debug payload logging is off unless explicitly enabled for an organization. When enabled, its default retention is 7 days.\n- Operational request logs contain metadata rather than payloads and have a default retention of 14 days.\n- Tracing spans linked to request IDs contain no payloads and have a default retention of 14 days.\n- For stored data in Redwood-managed systems, Redwood completes a verified deletion request within 30 days.\n- Changes to Redwood-managed retention require Security and SRE review and an update to the customer-facing Security FAQ.\n\nThese are product defaults, not substitutes for a customer's executed contract or an approved exception.\n\n## What Support must not promise yet\n\nThe reviewed published policy does not establish:\n\n- a backup or snapshot purge deadline;\n- a tenant-termination-specific purge deadline;\n- a data-residency or single-region guarantee;\n- whether backups remain in-region or replicate cross-region;\n- a standard deletion certificate, receipt, or audit-evidence package;\n- legal-hold exceptions or treatment of billing/control-plane metadata;\n- customer-configurable Hosted API retention beyond an approved, documented exception.\n\nSales calls and questionnaire emails contain materially different figures (including 30-day payload/log retention, 72-hour primary deletion, 14- to 90-day backup purge, and region-locking statements). Do not repeat those figures as general policy until Security/SRE and Legal validate them against current production behavior and contract templates.\n\n## Validation before answering a customer",

# Hosted API retention and deletion rule

Status: Support-facing interim rule (v1)
Owner: Platform & Console
Scope: Redwood-managed Hosted API

## What Support may state

- Customer content (prompts and outputs) is not stored persistently by default.
- Debug payload logging is off unless explicitly enabled for an organization. When enabled, its default retention is 7 days.
- Operational request logs contain metadata rather than payloads and have a default retention of 14 days.
- Tracing spans linked to request IDs contain no payloads and have a default retention of 14 days.
- For stored data in Redwood-managed systems, Redwood completes a verified deletion request within 30 days.
- Changes to Redwood-managed retention require Security and SRE review and an update to the customer-facing Security FAQ.

These are product defaults, not substitutes for a customer's executed contract or an approved exception.

## What Support must not promise yet

The reviewed published policy does not establish:

- a backup or snapshot purge deadline;
- a tenant-termination-specific purge deadline;
- a data-residency or single-region guarantee;
- whether backups remain in-region or replicate cross-region;
- a standard deletion certificate, receipt, or audit-evidence package;
- legal-hold exceptions or treatment of billing/control-plane metadata;
- customer-configurable Hosted API retention beyond an approved, documented exception.

Sales calls and questionnaire emails contain materially different figures (including 30-day payload/log retention, 72-hour primary deletion, 14- to 90-day backup purge, and region-locking statements). Do not repeat those figures as general policy until Security/SRE and Legal validate them against current production behavior and contract templates.

# Hosted API retention and deletion rule

Status: Support-facing interim rule (v1)
Owner: Platform & Console
Scope: Redwood-managed Hosted API

## What Support may state

- Customer content (prompts and outputs) is not stored persistently by default.
- Debug payload logging is off unless explicitly enabled for an organization. When enabled, its default retention is 7 days.
- Operational request logs contain metadata rather than payloads and have a default retention of 14 days.
- Tracing spans linked to request IDs contain no payloads and have a default retention of 14 days.
- For stored data in Redwood-managed systems, Redwood completes a verified deletion request within 30 days.
- Changes to Redwood-managed retention require Security and SRE review and an update to the customer-facing Security FAQ.

These are product defaults, not substitutes for a customer's executed contract or an approved exception.

## What Support must not promise yet

The reviewed published policy does not establish:

- a backup or snapshot purge deadline;
- a tenant-termination-specific purge deadline;
- a data-residency or single-region guarantee;
- whether backups remain in-region or replicate cross-region;
- a standard deletion certificate, receipt, or audit-evidence package;
- legal-hold exceptions or treatment of billing/control-plane metadata;
- customer-configurable Hosted API retention beyond an approved, documented exception.

Sales calls and questionnaire emails contain materially different figures (including 30-day payload/log retention, 72-hour primary deletion, 14- to 90-day backup purge, and region-locking statements). Do not repeat those figures as general policy until Security/SRE and Legal validate them against current production behavior and contract templates.

# Hosted API retention and deletion rule

Status: Support-facing interim rule (v1)
Owner: Platform & Console
Scope: Redwood-managed Hosted API

## What Support may state

- Customer content (prompts and outputs) is not stored persistently by default.
- Debug payload logging is off unless explicitly enabled for an organization. When enabled, its default retention is 7 days.
- Operational request logs contain metadata rather than payloads and have a default retention of 14 days.
- Tracing spans linked to request IDs contain no payloads and have a default retention of 14 days.
- For stored data in Redwood-managed systems, Redwood completes a verified deletion request within 30 days.
- Changes to Redwood-managed retention require Security and SRE review and an update to the customer-facing Security FAQ.

These are product defaults, not substitutes for a customer's executed contract or an approved exception.

## What Support must not promise yet

The reviewed published policy does not establish:

- a backup or snapshot purge deadline;
- a tenant-termination-specific purge deadline;
- a data-residency or single-region guarantee;
- whether backups remain in-region or replicate cross-region;
- a standard deletion certificate, receipt, or audit-evidence package;
- legal-hold exceptions or treatment of billing/control-plane metadata;
- customer-configurable Hosted API retention beyond an approved, documented exception.

Sales calls and questionnaire emails contain materially different figures (including 30-day payload/log retention, 72-hour primary deletion, 14- to 90-day backup purge, and region-locking statements). Do not repeat those figures as general policy until Security/SRE and Legal validate them against current production behavior and contract templates.

# Hosted API retention and deletion rule

Status: Support-facing interim rule (v1)
Owner: Platform & Console
Scope: Redwood-managed Hosted API

## What Support may state

- Customer content (prompts and outputs) is not stored persistently by default.
- Debug payload logging is off unless explicitly enabled for an organization. When enabled, its default retention is 7 days.
- Operational request logs contain metadata rather than payloads and have a default retention of 14 days.
- Tracing spans linked to request IDs contain no payloads and have a default retention of 14 days.
- For stored data in Redwood-managed systems, Redwood completes a verified deletion request within 30 days.
- Changes to Redwood-managed retention require Security and SRE review and an update to the customer-facing Security FAQ.

These are product defaults, not substitutes for a customer's executed contract or an approved exception.

## What Support must not promise yet

The reviewed published policy does not establish:

- a backup or snapshot purge deadline;
- a tenant-termination-specific purge deadline;
- a data-residency or single-region guarantee;
- whether backups remain in-region or replicate cross-region;
- a standard deletion certificate, receipt, or audit-evidence package;
- legal-hold exceptions or treatment of billing/control-plane metadata;
- customer-configurable Hosted API retention beyond an approved, documented exception.

Sales calls and questionnaire emails contain materially different figures (including 30-day payload/log retention, 72-hour primary deletion, 14- to 90-day backup purge, and region-locking statements). Do not repeat those figures as general policy until Security/SRE and Legal validate them against current production behavior and contract templates.

{
  "document": {
    "id": "dsid_c7f6ff2dcf674dd784e7f65c738d0724",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/tenant-decommission-and-data-erase-certification-playbook-2026.json",
    "title": "Tenant Decommission & Data Erasure Certification Playbook",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/confluence",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"Tenant Decommission & Data Erasure Certification Playbook\",\n  \"space\": \"customer-success-and-support\",\n  \"author\": \"Aisha Raman\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"customer-success\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-01-12\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2026-02-10\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Diego Morales\",\n    \"Priya Nair\",\n    \"Ethan Cole\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"decommission\",\n    \"data-retention\",\n    \"privacy\",\n    \"compliance\",\n    \"playbook\",\n    \"audit\"\n  ],\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"/confluence/customer-success-and-support/enterprise-onboarding/private-network-firewall-peering-checklist-2026\",\n    \"/confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/erase-certification-guidelines-2025\"\n  ],\n  \"confidentiality\": \"restricted\",\n  \"body\": \"Summary:\\nThis playbook defines the operational process, verification steps, and evidence collection required to safely decommission a tenant and produce a Data Erasure Certification for enterprise customers. It is intended for Customer Success Engineers (CSEs), Site Reliability Engineers (SREs), Account Security leads, and the Privacy Compliance team.\\n\\nScope:\\n- Applies to all Dedicated and Private tenants (reserved capacity or VPC/on-prem) where a customer requests a full tenant decommission and verified data purge.\\n- Excludes transient test tenants created under internal dev projects.\\n- Covers: configuration metadata, KV caches, embedding indices, logs and telemetry tied to tenant IDs, backups/snapshots, and any customer-managed on-prem artifacts we control.\\n\\nGoals:\\n- Ensure data belonging to a tenant is irrecoverably deleted from all Redwood-managed storage within agreed SLA windows.\\n- Produce a signed Data Erasure Certification (PDF) including verification artifacts suitable for customer audit.\\n- Provide a clear rollback and exception path if deletion interferes with legal holds, active billing disputes, or regulatory constraints.\\n\\nPrerequisites and gating checks (Pre-decommission):\\n1) Confirm formal request: must come from the customer\\u2019s authorized admin contact or a signed CSM request form. Attach request to ticket.\\n2) Confirm account state: Tenant must be quiesced for at least 48 hours unless an accelerated erase is explicitly authorized by Legal.\\n3) Verify no active legal holds or retention policies: Check Legal/Evidence mailbox and related JIRA signals.\\n4) Snapshot list: Enumerate all active snapshots, backups, and object storage buckets that contain tenant data.\\n5) Billing & contracts: Finance must sign off that invoicing and reconciliations are complete, or place a hold if a dispute exists.\\n\\nRoles and responsibilities:\\n- Customer Success Engineer (CSE): owner of the decommission process, customer comms, and final handoff of the certification.\\n- SRE / Infra Owner: executes deletion commands, validates low-level storage and KV cache removal, updates runbook evidence.\\n- Privacy & Compliance: reviews evidence, prepares certification language, and signs final PDF.\\n- Account Security Lead: verifies no remaining credentials, SSH keys, certificates, or cross-tenant links.\\n- Finance: confirms final billing state.\\n\\nHigh-level decommission checklist (stepwise):\\n1) Prepare: Create a decommission incident ticket (PREFIX: DECOM-{tenant_id}) and add all owners and reviewers. Attach customer request and any hold flags.\\n2) Quiesce: Disable API keys, revoke incoming webhooks, and switch routing policy to reject new traffic. Record timestamps.\\n3) Export minimal retention artefacts (if requested): generate requested audit logs and export them to a customer-managed bucket; document the export SHA256.\\n4) Snapshot verification: Ensure latest snapshot is stored in immutable archive (if contractually required). Note location and checksum.\\n5) Delete operational artifacts (order matters):\\n   a) Revoke and purge tenant IAM roles and tokens.\\n   b) Remove routing and DNS entries.\\n   c) Stop and delete serving instances (record instance IDs).\\n   d) Wipe KV caches and in-memory stores with secure-delete commands.\\n   e) Delete embedding indices and associated vector DB partitions.\\n   f) Remove object storage buckets and blobs.\\n   g) Delete logs and telemetry for tenant IDs (respecting retention law exceptions).\\n6) Cease backups: ensure backup jobs no longer include tenant and delete retained backup files.\\n7) Final storage sweep: run storage-level compliance scan to find orphaned objects or references.\\n8) Evidence collection: collect command outputs, checksums, S3 / object delete receipts, and storage listings that show 404/NotFound.\\n9) Generate Draft Certification: Privacy prepares draft certification with attached evidence links.\\n10) Sign-off: Legal/Privacy and Finance must approve. Once approved, deliver signed PDF to customer via secure channel and close the decommission ticket.\\n\\nCommands and verification examples (examples - replace with tenant values):\\n- Revoke API keys (CLI): redwood-cli tenants revoke-keys --tenant-id tenant-123 --force\\n- KV cache wipe (runbook snippet): curl -X POST https://kv.internal.redwood/delete-namespace -d '{\\\"tenant\\\":\\\"tenant-123\\\",\\\"mode\\\":\\\"secure\\\"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <ops-token>'\\n- Object store delete + verification (bash):\\n  aws s3 rm s3://redwood-tenants/tenant-123 --recursive && aws s3 ls s3://redwood-tenants/tenant-123 || echo \\\"Bucket not found\\\"\\n- Snapshot checksum (example): sha256sum tenant-123-snapshot-20260101.tar.gz > snapshot.sha256\\n\\nEvidence packaging requirements:\\n- Include: ticket export, customer request, command stdout logs (with timestamps), storage deletion receipts, backup job logs, checksum files, and the pre-decommission inventory.\\n- Redact: Do not include PII of Redwood employees in delivered artifacts. Replace internal ticket IDs with redacted tokens when necessary.\\n- Evidence TTL: Internal evidence must be retained in the audited evidence bucket for 2 years (Compliance mandate).\\n\\nVerification checklist (to be ticked in ticket):\\n- [ ] Customer request attached and validated against admin contact.\\n- [ ] Quiesce actions completed and timestamped.\\n- [ ] All API keys and webhooks revoked.\\n- [ ] Embedding indices removed and index count = 0.\\n- [ ] Object storage bucket returns NotFound.\\n- [ ] Backups and snapshots removed or archived as per contract.\\n- [ ] KV cache namespace removed and confirmed.\\n- [ ] Logs trimmed or removed respecting legal holds.\\n- [ ] Privacy & Legal sign-off obtained.\\n- [ ] Signed Data Erasure Certification produced and delivered.\\n\\nRollback and exceptions:\\n- Legal Hold: If a legal hold is identified mid-process, immediately pause deletion steps and notify Legal and the customer. Rehydrate any removed snapshots from immutable archive if possible.\\n- Accidental deletion: If accidental deletion is detected within the retention window, follow the Incident Recovery Runbook (link in related_pages) and escalate to SRE Lead and CTO on-call.\\n- Customer Revocation: Customer may revoke the decommission within the quiesce window if approved; in that case, restore routing and reactivate keys following the Tenant Reactivation checklist.\\n\\nCommunication templates (summary snippets to use in ticket and email):\\n- Initial acknowledgement to customer: \\\"We have received your decommission request. The tenant has been scheduled for quiesce on {date}. Expected completion: {date + X business days}. We will provide a Data Erasure Certification when the process completes.\\\"\\n- Final delivery message: \\\"Attached is your Data Erasure Certification for tenant {tenant_id}. This confirms Redwood-managed artifacts have been erased per the contract. Contact your CSM with any audit questions.\\\"\\n\\nAudit and certification content (what we include in the PDF):\\n- Statement of scope (tenant id, dates, artifacts included/excluded).\\n- Listing of deleted artifact types and counts (buckets deleted, indices removed, instances terminated).\\n- Verification artifacts (checksums, deletion receipts, ticket references).\\n- Signatures: Privacy & Compliance lead + CSE.\\n- Optional: a notarized stamp if requested and pre-approved by Legal (adds 3-7 business days).\\n\\nOperational metrics and SLAs for decommission requests:\\n- Standard FIFO SLA: 10 business days from validated request to certified completion.\\n- Accelerated SLA: 48\\u201396 hours (requires signed acceleration waiver from customer and Legal approval).\\n- Verification SLA: Privacy has 5 business days to review and sign evidence once uploaded.\\n\\nAutomation and tools:\\n- Decommission Orchestrator (internal service): Use the decommission orchestration UI for walk-through steps and to collect structured evidence. If the orchestrator is unavailable, follow the manual runbook steps above.\\n- Evidence bucket: s3://redwood-evidence/decom/tenant-{tenant_id}/{ticket_id}/\\n- Template generator: internal tool that assembles evidence links into the draft certification.\\n\\nPost-decommission monitoring (30 days):\\n- Watch for retroactive billing anomalies or customer follow-ups. Set a 30-day ticket cooling period where CSE monitors any reappearance of tenant artifacts.\\n- Run a weekly orphan-object scan for the tenant id for 4 weeks post-deletion and archive results into the ticket.\\n\\nAppendices:\\nA) Example minimal Data Erasure Certification language (copy into PDF generator):\\n\\\"Redwood Inference certifies that, as of {date}, Redwood-managed storage and runtime artifacts associated with tenant {tenant_id} were deleted and validated in accordance with the contract and Redwood internal data retention policies. Evidence artifacts are appended/linked in this certification. Signed: {PrivacyLead}, {CSEName}.\\\"\\n\\nB) Quick checklist for small tenants (one-liner):\\n1) Verify request -> 2) Revoke keys -> 3) Delete bucket -> 4) Remove indices -> 5) Deliver certification.\\n\\nC) Emergency contacts:\\n- Customer Success Incident Pager: +1-555-0123 (internal)\\n- Privacy & Compliance Slack: #privacy-compliance (tag @privacy-lead)\\n- SRE On-call: see internal roster or PagerDuty schedule\\n\\nChange log:\\n- 2026-01-12: Playbook created by Aisha Raman.\\n- 2026-01-25: Added accelerated SLA flow and notarization note (review by Legal).\\n- 2026-02-10: Clarified evidence TTL and added orphan-object weekly-scan requirement (reviewers: Diego Morales, Priya Nair).\\n\\nRelated references and links:\\n- Tenant quiesce runbook: /confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/scheduled-tenant-quiesce-and-safe-failback-playbook-2026\\n- Data residency & retention policy: /confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/policy-2025\\n- Incident recovery runbook: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks/incident-recovery-2025\\n\\nOwner and contact:\\n- Playbook owner: Aisha Raman (CSE Lead) - aisha.r@redwood.ai\\n- Privacy reviewer: Priya Nair - priya.n@redwood.ai\\n- SRE liaison: Diego Morales - diego.m@redwood.ai\\n\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"body\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_c7f6ff2dcf674dd784e7f65c738d0724\"\n}",
