document.title: Tenant Decommission & Data Erasure Certification Playbook
document.content:
{
  "title": "Tenant Decommission & Data Erasure Certification Playbook",
  "space": "customer-success-and-support",
  "author": "Aisha Raman",
  "owner_team": "customer-success",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2026-01-12",
  "last_updated": "2026-02-10",
  "reviewers": [
    "Diego Morales",
    "Priya Nair",
    "Ethan Cole"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "decommission",
    "data-retention",
    "privacy",
    "compliance",
    "playbook",
    "audit"
  ],
  "related_pages": [
    "/confluence/customer-success-and-support/enterprise-onboarding/private-network-firewall-peering-checklist-2026",
    "/confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/erase-certification-guidelines-2025"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "restricted",
  "body": "Summary:
This playbook defines the operational process, verification steps, and evidence collection required to safely decommission a tenant and produce a Data Erasure Certification for enterprise customers. It is intended for Customer Success Engineers (CSEs), Site Reliability Engineers (SREs), Account Security leads, and the Privacy Compliance team.

Scope:
- Applies to all Dedicated and Private tenants (reserved capacity or VPC/on-prem) where a customer requests a full tenant decommission and verified data purge.
- Excludes transient test tenants created under internal dev projects.
- Covers: configuration metadata, KV caches, embedding indices, logs and telemetry tied to tenant IDs, backups/snapshots, and any customer-managed on-prem artifacts we control.

Goals:
- Ensure data belonging to a tenant is irrecoverably deleted from all Redwood-managed storage within agreed SLA windows.
- Produce a signed Data Erasure Certification (PDF) including verification artifacts suitable for customer audit.
- Provide a clear rollback and exception path if deletion interferes with legal holds, active billing disputes, or regulatory constraints.

Prerequisites and gating checks (Pre-decommission):
1) Confirm formal request: must come from the customer’s authorized admin contact or a signed CSM request form. Attach request to ticket.
2) Confirm account state: Tenant must be quiesced for at least 48 hours unless an accelerated erase is explicitly authorized by Legal.
3) Verify no active legal holds or retention policies: Check Legal/Evidence mailbox and related JIRA signals.
4) Snapshot list: Enumerate all active snapshots, backups, and object storage buckets that contain tenant data.
5) Billing & contracts: Finance must sign off that invoicing and reconciliations are complete, or place a hold if a dispute exists.

Roles and responsibilities:
- Customer Success Engineer (CSE): owner of the decommission process, customer comms, and final handoff of the certification.
- SRE / Infra Owner: executes deletion commands, validates low-level storage and KV cache removal, updates runbook evidence.
- Privacy & Compliance: reviews evidence, prepares certification language, and signs final PDF.
- Account Security Lead: verifies no remaining credentials, SSH keys, certificates, or cross-tenant links.
- Finance: confirms final billing state.

High-level decommission checklist (stepwise):
1) Prepare: Create a decommission incident ticket (PREFIX: DECOM-{tenant_id}) and add all owners and reviewers. Attach customer request and any hold flags.
2) Quiesce: Disable API keys, revoke incoming webhooks, and switch routing policy to reject new traffic. Record timestamps.
3) Export minimal retention artefacts (if requested): generate requested audit logs and export them to a customer-managed bucket; document the export SHA256.
4) Snapshot verification: Ensure latest snapshot is stored in immutable archive (if contractually required). Note location and checksum.
5) Delete operational artifacts (order matters):
   a) Revoke and purge tenant IAM roles and tokens.
   b) Remove routing and DNS entries.
   c) Stop and delete serving instances (record instance IDs).
   d) Wipe KV caches and in-memory stores with secure-delete commands.
   e) Delete embedding indices and associated vector DB partitions.
   f) Remove object storage buckets and blobs.
   g) Delete logs and telemetry for tenant IDs (respecting retention law exceptions).
6) Cease backups: ensure backup jobs no longer include tenant and delete retained backup files.
7) Final storage sweep: run storage-level compliance scan to find orphaned objects or references.
8) Evidence collection: collect command outputs, checksums, S3 / object delete receipts, and storage listings that show 404/NotFound.
9) Generate Draft Certification: Privacy prepares draft certification with attached evidence links.
10) Sign-off: Legal/Privacy and Finance must approve. Once approved, deliver signed PDF to customer via secure channel and close the decommission ticket.

Commands and verification examples (examples - replace with tenant values):
- Revoke API keys (CLI): redwood-cli tenants revoke-keys --tenant-id tenant-123 --force
- KV cache wipe (runbook snippet): curl -X POST https://kv.internal.redwood/delete-namespace -d '{"tenant":"tenant-123","mode":"secure"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <ops-token>'
- Object store delete + verification (bash):
  aws s3 rm s3://redwood-tenants/tenant-123 --recursive && aws s3 ls s3://redwood-tenants/tenant-123 || echo "Bucket not found"
- Snapshot checksum (example): sha256sum tenant-123-snapshot-20260101.tar.gz > snapshot.sha256

Evidence packaging requirements:
- Include: ticket export, customer request, command stdout logs (with timestamps), storage deletion receipts, backup job logs, checksum files, and the pre-decommission inventory.
- Redact: Do not include PII of Redwood employees in delivered artifacts. Replace internal ticket IDs with redacted tokens when necessary.
- Evidence TTL: Internal evidence must be retained in the audited evidence bucket for 2 years (Compliance mandate).

Verification checklist (to be ticked in ticket):
- [ ] Customer request attached and validated against admin contact.
- [ ] Quiesce actions completed and timestamped.
- [ ] All API keys and webhooks revoked.
- [ ] Embedding indices removed and index count = 0.
- [ ] Object storage bucket returns NotFound.
- [ ] Backups and snapshots removed or archived as per contract.
- [ ] KV cache namespace removed and confirmed.
- [ ] Logs trimmed or removed respecting legal holds.
- [ ] Privacy & Legal sign-off obtained.
- [ ] Signed Data Erasure Certification produced and delivered.

Rollback and exceptions:
- Legal Hold: If a legal hold is identified mid-process, immediately pause deletion steps and notify Legal and the customer. Rehydrate any removed snapshots from immutable archive if possible.
- Accidental deletion: If accidental deletion is detected within the retention window, follow the Incident Recovery Runbook (link in related_pages) and escalate to SRE Lead and CTO on-call.
- Customer Revocation: Customer may revoke the decommission within the quiesce window if approved; in that case, restore routing and reactivate keys following the Tenant Reactivation checklist.

Communication templates (summary snippets to use in ticket and email):
- Initial acknowledgement to customer: "We have received your decommission request. The tenant has been scheduled for quiesce on {date}. Expected completion: {date + X business days}. We will provide a Data Erasure Certification when the process completes."
- Final delivery message: "Attached is your Data Erasure Certification for tenant {tenant_id}. This confirms Redwood-managed artifacts have been erased per the contract. Contact your CSM with any audit questions."

Audit and certification content (what we include in the PDF):
- Statement of scope (tenant id, dates, artifacts included/excluded).
- Listing of deleted artifact types and counts (buckets deleted, indices removed, instances terminated).
- Verification artifacts (checksums, deletion receipts, ticket references).
- Signatures: Privacy & Compliance lead + CSE.
- Optional: a notarized stamp if requested and pre-approved by Legal (adds 3-7 business days).

Operational metrics and SLAs for decommission requests:
- Standard FIFO SLA: 10 business days from validated request to certified completion.
- Accelerated SLA: 48–96 hours (requires signed acceleration waiver from customer and Legal approval).
- Verification SLA: Privacy has 5 business days to review and sign evidence once uploaded.

Automation and tools:
- Decommission Orchestrator (internal service): Use the decommission orchestration UI for walk-through steps and to collect structured evidence. If the orchestrator is unavailable, follow the manual runbook steps above.
- Evidence bucket: s3://redwood-evidence/decom/tenant-{tenant_id}/{ticket_id}/
- Template generator: internal tool that assembles evidence links into the draft certification.

Post-decommission monitoring (30 days):
- Watch for retroactive billing anomalies or customer follow-ups. Set a 30-day ticket cooling period where CSE monitors any reappearance of tenant artifacts.
- Run a weekly orphan-object scan for the tenant id for 4 weeks post-deletion and archive results into the ticket.

Appendices:
A) Example minimal Data Erasure Certification language (copy into PDF generator):
"Redwood Inference certifies that, as of {date}, Redwood-managed storage and runtime artifacts associated with tenant {tenant_id} were deleted and validated in accordance with the contract and Redwood internal data retention policies. Evidence artifacts are appended/linked in this certification. Signed: {PrivacyLead}, {CSEName}."

B) Quick checklist for small tenants (one-liner):
1) Verify request -> 2) Revoke keys -> 3) Delete bucket -> 4) Remove indices -> 5) Deliver certification.

C) Emergency contacts:
- Customer Success Incident Pager: +1-555-0123 (internal)
- Privacy & Compliance Slack: #privacy-compliance (tag @privacy-lead)
- SRE On-call: see internal roster or PagerDuty schedule

Change log:
- 2026-01-12: Playbook created by Aisha Raman.
- 2026-01-25: Added accelerated SLA flow and notarization note (review by Legal).
- 2026-02-10: Clarified evidence TTL and added orphan-object weekly-scan requirement (reviewers: Diego Morales, Priya Nair).

Related references and links:
- Tenant quiesce runbook: /confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/scheduled-tenant-quiesce-and-safe-failback-playbook-2026
- Data residency & retention policy: /confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/policy-2025
- Incident recovery runbook: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks/incident-recovery-2025

Owner and contact:
- Playbook owner: Aisha Raman (CSE Lead) - aisha.r@redwood.ai
- Privacy reviewer: Priya Nair - priya.n@redwood.ai
- SRE liaison: Diego Morales - diego.m@redwood.ai

  "content_field_names": [
    "body"
  ],

}

  "title": "Hosted Data Residency Policy and Engineering Controls",
  "space": "security-and-compliance",
  "author": "Olga Petrov",
  "owner_team": "security",
  "status": "published",
  "confidentiality": "restricted (security/legal/customer-sensitive)",
  "created_at": "2025-01-22",
  "last_updated": "2025-03-07",
  "reviewers": [
    "Dr. Aisha Rahman",
    "Marcus Lin",
    "Naomi Feldman",
    "Sean Gallagher",
    "Amara Diallo"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "data-residency",
    "hosted-api",
    "security-policy",
    "soc2",
    "iso27001",
    "controls",
    "enterprise"
  ],
  "related_pages": [
    "adr-021-region-pinning-enforcement-boundaries",
    "adr-022-error-contract-for-residency-violations",

    "data-residency-enforcement-monitoring",
    "runbook-residency-enforcement-false-positives"
  ],
  "body": "## 1. Purpose\nThis document defines Redwood Inference\u2019s internal policy for **Hosted API data residency** and the required **engineering and operational controls** used to enforce it. It is written to:\n- Provide a clear, auditable statement of what residency guarantees are provided for Hosted API.\n- Define enforcement boundaries (what counts as \u201ccustomer content\u201d and what must remain in-region).\n- Specify required controls across routing, fallback behavior, logging/telemetry, and background processing.\n- Map controls to common compliance frameworks (SOC 2 and ISO/IEC 27001) for audit narratives.\n\nThis policy supports the Enterprise Security & Compliance Foundation initiative: **Hosted data residency enforcement (region pinning)**.\n\n## 2. Scope\n### 2.1 In scope\n- **Redwood Hosted API** request handling for text generation/chat, embeddings, reranking, and streaming/non-streaming variants.\n- Request routing and model selection (**Smart Routing**) and related fallback behavior.\n- API request validation and error responses (**API Gateway**).\n- Logging and telemetry systems that may contain customer content (application logs, traces, debug payloads).\n- Background processing directly triggered by Hosted API requests (e.g., asynchronous request completion, retry workers, moderation/classification where applicable).\n- Administrative configuration for residency policies (**Residency Policy Service** in the control plane).\n\n### 2.2 Out of scope (initial release)\n- Automatic multi-region replication of customer data.\n- Advanced geo-fencing beyond request routing and logging boundaries (handled via phased hardening).\n- Customer-managed encryption key residency guarantees (covered separately under key management policy).\n- Dedicated and Private deployments (covered under separate service-specific residency statements; Dedicated may implement aligned region selection but is not governed by Hosted control plane policy objects unless explicitly configured).\n\n## 3. Definitions\n### 3.1 Residency terms\n- **Region**: A public cloud region (e.g., eu-west-1) mapped to a Redwood internal region identifier (e.g., EU1). Region mapping is maintained by Platform Engineering (see internal region mapping sheet).\n- **Allowed regions**: The set of regions in which customer content is permitted to be processed for an org/project/API key.\n- **Primary region**: The default region for routing when multiple regions are allowed.\n- **Region pinning**: A configuration that restricts Hosted API processing to an allowed region set.\n\n### 3.2 Customer content (enforcement boundary)\nFor this policy, **customer content** includes:\n- Request prompts/messages, tool/function payloads, and attachments that are provided to the model.\n- Model outputs (tokens, completions, embeddings vectors derived from customer-provided input).\n- Customer-provided metadata that can contain sensitive data (e.g., \u201cuser_message\u201d, \u201ccontext\u201d, \u201cdocuments\u201d).\n- Any derived artifacts that include reconstructable content (e.g., cached prefixes/KV cache entries, debug dumps).\n\nCustomer content does **not** include:\n- Non-content operational metadata that does not contain sensitive data (e.g., request_id, org_id, project_id, model_id, region_id, error_code, timestamps, latency metrics).\n\nNote: These boundaries must match ADR-021 \u201cRegion Pinning Enforcement Boundaries\u201d. Where ambiguity exists, classify as customer content.\n\n## 4. Policy statement (what we guarantee)\n### 4.1 Hosted residency guarantee\nIf an organization/project/API key is configured with an allowed region set, Redwood guarantees that:\n1) **Processing location**: Customer content for Hosted API requests will be processed only in the allowed region(s).\n2) **No cross-region fallback with content**: Routing and fallback behavior will not send customer content to a region outside the allowed set.\n3) **Deterministic enforcement**: Requests that would violate policy are blocked at request time (or at the earliest deterministic point for streaming) with a consistent error contract.\n4) **Logging/telemetry boundaries**: Systems that could store customer content (including traces and debug logs) will store such content only in the allowed region(s) or will be content-redacted before leaving the region.\n5) **Administrative auditability**: Changes to residency configuration are recorded in audit logs with actor, timestamp, and change details.\n\n### 4.2 Supported residency modes\n- **Single-region pin**: Allowed regions contains exactly one region (e.g., EU-only).\n- **Multi-region allowed set**: Allowed regions contains multiple regions (e.g., EU + UK) with a primary.\n- **No pinning**: Default routing behavior applies; residency guarantee does not apply.\n\n### 4.3 Precedence rules (which policy applies)\nPolicy precedence is:\n1) API key-level policy (most specific)\n2) Project-level policy\n3) Org-level policy (least specific)\n4) No residency policy\n\nIf conflicting policies exist, the most specific applicable policy is used.\n\n## 5. Explicit exclusions / limitations\nThe following are excluded from the Hosted residency guarantee unless contractually stated otherwise and implemented under separate controls:\n- **Client-side routing**: If customers send requests to a region-specific endpoint that is not in their allowed set, the request will be blocked; Redwood does not control customer network paths.\n- **Customer-managed storage**: Content that customers export/download/store in their own systems is outside Redwood\u2019s residency scope.\n- **Third-party processors outside region**: If a customer enables optional integrations that transmit content externally (e.g., webhooks to their own endpoints), residency depends on customer configuration.\n- **Support workflows**: Support will not request raw customer prompts/outputs for troubleshooting unless explicitly approved by the customer and handled via approved secure channels; such handling is governed by Support Data Handling Policy.\n- **Aggregated metrics**: Non-content operational metrics may be stored in centralized systems outside the pinned region (see Section 7.4). Metrics must not include customer content.\n- **Model provider constraints**: For hosted open models running on Redwood-managed infrastructure, processing occurs in-region; if any future offering involves third-party model endpoints, it must be explicitly excluded or separately controlled and disclosed.\n\n## 6. Control objectives\nControls must meet these objectives:\n- **CO-1 (Policy correctness)**: The evaluated policy matches configured intent and is consistent across gateway and routing.\n- **CO-2 (Enforcement)**: Any routing decision that would move customer content out of allowed regions is blocked.\n- **CO-3 (Observability)**: Residency decisions and blocks are observable without leaking customer content.\n- **CO-4 (Auditability)**: Config changes are logged and retrievable for auditors and incident response.\n- **CO-5 (Operational safety)**: Enforcement failures default to a safe posture (block or in-region), with clear incident procedures.\n\n## 7. Required engineering controls\n### 7.1 Control plane: Residency Policy Service\n**Requirement:** Residency policy objects must be stored and served by the control plane with authorization and validation.\n\nMinimum requirements:\n- AuthZ: Only authorized org/project admins (and internal admin roles) can create/update/delete policies.\n- Validation:\n  - allowed_regions must be a non-empty list when policy is enabled.\n  - primary_region must be a member of allowed_regions.\n  - Regions must be valid and currently supported for Hosted.\n- Change control:\n  - Mutations must emit an **audit log event**.\n  - Policy versions must be retrievable (history) for internal investigations.\n\n### 7.2 API Gateway: request-time validation & error contract\n**Requirement:** The gateway must validate residency policy before forwarding request content to downstream systems.\n\n- The gateway fetches or is provided residency policy context (policy_id, allowed_regions, primary_region, enforcement_mode).\n- If the incoming request is targeted to or would be processed in a disallowed region, the gateway must block.\n- Errors must follow the public error contract (ADR-022):\n  - HTTP status code: **409 Conflict** (policy conflict) for residency violations.\n  - Machine-readable error code (example): `residency_policy_violation`.\n  - Response includes `request_id` and a stable `help_url`.\n  - Response must not include customer content.\n\nStreaming: If streaming starts, the system must not stream any model output if the request later evaluates as disallowed. Residency evaluation must be performed before tokens are generated.\n\n### 7.3 Smart Routing: region selection and fallback constraints\n**Requirement:** Routing decisions must treat residency as a hard constraint.\n\nRules:\n- Candidate regions = allowed_regions (if policy exists) else default routing regions.\n- Primary region is selected when healthy and capacity is available.\n- Failover/fallback is permitted **only** within allowed_regions.\n- Cross-region fallback outside allowed_regions is prohibited unless an explicit, customer-configured exception exists (see Section 10).\n\nRouting must emit a structured **residency decision context** into logs/telemetry:\n- request_id, org_id, project_id\n- evaluated_policy_id (if any)\n- allowed_regions\n- selected_region\n- decision_outcome: allow | block\n- block_reason (if block)\n\n### 7.4 Logging, telemetry, and tracing\n**Requirement:** Customer content must not leave the allowed region via logs/traces.\n\nControls:\n- Content redaction: Default logging configuration must redact customer content fields. Any \u201cdebug logging\u201d that includes content must be region-scoped storage and gated behind time-limited feature flags with Security approval.\n- Trace payloads: Traces may include identifiers and timing but must not include prompt text, generated text, or embedding vectors.\n- Central metrics: Aggregated counters/histograms may be centrally stored cross-region if they contain no customer content (e.g., counts by error_code, latency percentiles, block rate).\n- Residency decision logs: Must not include raw prompts/outputs; only structured metadata.\n\n### 7.5 Caching and intermediate artifacts\n**Requirement:** Any caching that may contain customer content (prefix/KV caches, request replay buffers) must be region-local.\n\n- Cache keys and values must not replicate across regions.\n- Cache warming strategies must not copy customer content cross-region.\n- For shared multi-tenant caches, tenant isolation controls still apply; residency adds region isolation.\n\n### 7.6 Background processing and retries\n**Requirement:** Background tasks triggered by Hosted requests must execute in-region.\n\n- Retry workers must be region-affine.\n- Queueing systems must not move message payloads (containing content) outside region.\n- Any exception must be treated as a residency incident.\n\n### 7.7 Security testing and release gates\n**Requirement:** Residency enforcement must be validated with automated and manual tests.\n\nMinimum gates:\n- E2E tests:\n  - Pinned EU org sending traffic that would route to US must be blocked with correct error contract.\n  - Streaming endpoint returns standardized residency error (not generic 5xx).\n  - Cross-region fallback attempts are prevented.\n- Negative testing:\n  - Invalid policy configs rejected.\n  - Missing/unknown region IDs handled safely (block or default-safe per design).\n- Change review: Any code change that touches residency evaluation, routing, logging, or policy schema must be reviewed by Security Engineering.\n\n### 7.8 Monitoring and alerting\n**Requirement:** SRE-owned dashboards and alerts must exist for residency enforcement.\n\nAt minimum:\n- Blocked requests count and rate by region, by org tier.\n- Policy evaluation latency (p95/p99) to ensure enforcement does not introduce outages.\n- Cross-region routing attempt counter.\n- Error rate deltas after rollout by region.\n\nPaging guidance:\n- Page SRE on sustained spikes in `residency_policy_violation` that exceed baseline and correlate with customer impact.\n- Page Security on any signal suggesting content may have been processed outside allowed regions.\n\n## 8. Compliance mapping (SOC 2 / ISO 27001)\nThis section provides narrative mapping; exact auditor evidence is maintained in the \u201cData Residency Enforcement Evidence Pack v1\u201d.\n\n### 8.1 SOC 2 (Trust Services Criteria) mapping\n- **CC6 (Logical and physical access controls)**\n  - Control: AuthZ for Residency Policy Service mutations; admin RBAC; audit logs for changes.\n  - Evidence: policy change audit events; access review records.\n- **CC7 (System operations and change management)**\n  - Control: Monitoring/alerting for blocks and anomalies; incident runbooks; release gates and testing.\n  - Evidence: dashboards, alerts, incident tickets, CI results.\n- **CC8 (Change management)**\n  - Control: Peer review, Security review requirement, controlled rollout with feature flags.\n  - Evidence: PR approvals, rollout plans, change records.\n- **A1 (Availability)**\n  - Control: Fail-closed behavior; in-region fallback only; capacity monitoring.\n  - Evidence: routing logs showing selection within allowed regions; SLO reporting.\n\n### 8.2 ISO/IEC 27001 mapping (illustrative)\n- **A.5 / A.6 (Governance and roles)**\n  - Policy ownership by Security; defined responsibilities across Platform/SRE.\n- **A.8 (Asset management / information classification)**\n  - Definition of customer content and handling requirements.\n- **A.12 (Operations security)**\n  - Monitoring, logging controls, secure operation of region-scoped systems.\n- **A.14 (System acquisition, development, maintenance)**\n  - SDLC gates, security review, testing.\n- **A.16 (Incident management)**\n  - Runbook for false positives and residency incidents; escalation paths.\n\n## 9. Roles and responsibilities\n- **Security Engineering (Marcus Lin)**: defines security requirements; reviews enforcement boundary changes; leads investigations of potential residency breaches.\n- **GRC (Olga Petrov)**: maintains this policy; prepares evidence packs; supports audits and questionnaires.\n- **Product (Naomi Feldman)**: owns customer-facing commitments and documentation alignment.\n- **Platform Control Plane (Ethan Park)**: owns policy service implementation, validation, and migrations.\n- **API Gateway (Amara Diallo / Brian Murphy)**: owns request-time enforcement and public error contract.\n- **Routing (Mina Haddad / Ravi Menon)**: owns routing constraints and fallback behavior.\n- **SRE (Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes)**: owns monitoring, alerts, on-call readiness, and rollback procedures.\n\n## 10. Exceptions and emergency procedures\n### 10.1 Customer exceptions\nAny exception to allow cross-region processing for a pinned customer must be:\n- Explicitly requested by the customer in writing, with scope and duration.\n- Approved by Security Engineering and the Product owner.\n- Implemented as a configuration flag with an expiry date and audit log entries.\n\n### 10.2 Internal emergency override\nEmergency override (e.g., to mitigate broad false positives) is permitted only when:\n- The override does not result in processing customer content outside allowed regions.\n- If the only way to restore service would violate residency, the correct action is to **block** rather than route cross-region.\n\nAll overrides must:\n- Be time-bound (default max 2 hours) and logged.\n- Trigger a post-incident review.\n\n## 11. Evidence and audit readiness\nMinimum evidence artifacts maintained per release:\n- Policy schema and validation documentation.\n- ADR-021 and ADR-022.\n- Screenshots/links to dashboards and alerts.\n- Sample structured residency decision logs (content-redacted).\n- Audit log samples for policy create/update/delete.\n- E2E test results demonstrating block behavior and non-cross-region fallback.\n\nRetention of evidence follows Security Compliance Evidence Retention Policy.\n\n## 12. Review cadence\n- This policy must be reviewed **at least annually** or upon material changes to:\n  - Regions supported for Hosted\n  - Logging/tracing architecture\n  - Routing/fallback design\n  - Customer-facing residency commitments\n\nPolicy owner: GRC (Olga Petrov). Technical approver: CISO (Dr. Aisha Rahman).\n\n## 13. Appendix: Standard error behavior (internal summary)\nWhen a request is blocked due to residency:\n- Status: 409\n- error_code: residency_policy_violation\n- message: indicates selected/target region is not in allowed set (no customer content)\n- includes: request_id, help_url\n- logging: decision context only; no prompt/output\n\nFor exact payload fields and SDK behavior, refer to ADR-022.\n",

{
  "title": "Hosted Data Residency Policy and Engineering Controls",
  "space": "security-and-compliance",
  "author": "Olga Petrov",
  "owner_team": "security",
  "status": "published",
  "confidentiality": "restricted (security/legal/customer-sensitive)",
  "created_at": "2025-01-22",
  "last_updated": "2025-03-07",
  "reviewers": [
    "Dr. Aisha Rahman",
    "Marcus Lin",
    "Naomi Feldman",
    "Sean Gallagher",
    "Amara Diallo"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "data-residency",
    "hosted-api",
    "security-policy",
    "soc2",
    "iso27001",
    "controls",
    "enterprise"
  ],
  "related_pages": [
    "adr-021-region-pinning-enforcement-boundaries",
    "adr-022-error-contract-for-residency-violations",
    "residency-policy-service",
    "data-residency-enforcement-monitoring",
    "runbook-residency-enforcement-false-positives"
  ],
  "body": "## 1. Purpose
This document defines Redwood Inference’s internal policy for **Hosted API data residency** and the required **engineering and operational controls** used to enforce it. It is written to:
- Provide a clear, auditable statement of what residency guarantees are provided for Hosted API.
- Define enforcement boundaries (what counts as “customer content” and what must remain in-region).
- Specify required controls across routing, fallback behavior, logging/telemetry, and background processing.
- Map controls to common compliance frameworks (SOC 2 and ISO/IEC 27001) for audit narratives.

This policy supports the Enterprise Security & Compliance Foundation initiative: **Hosted data residency enforcement (region pinning)**.

## 2. Scope
### 2.1 In scope
- **Redwood Hosted API** request handling for text generation/chat, embeddings, reranking, and streaming/non-streaming variants.
- Request routing and model selection (**Smart Routing**) and related fallback behavior.
- API request validation and error responses (**API Gateway**).
- Logging and telemetry systems that may contain customer content (application logs, traces, debug payloads).
- Background processing directly triggered by Hosted API requests (e.g., asynchronous request completion, retry workers, moderation/classification where applicable).
- Administrative configuration for residency policies (**Residency Policy Service** in the control plane).

### 2.2 Out of scope (initial release)
- Automatic multi-region replication of customer data.
- Advanced geo-fencing beyond request routing and logging boundaries (handled via phased hardening).
- Customer-managed encryption key residency guarantees (covered separately under key management policy).
- Dedicated and Private deployments (covered under separate service-specific residency statements; Dedicated may implement aligned region selection but is not governed by Hosted control plane policy objects unless explicitly configured).

## 3. Definitions
### 3.1 Residency terms
- **Region**: A public cloud region (e.g., eu-west-1) mapped to a Redwood internal region identifier (e.g., EU1). Region mapping is maintained by Platform Engineering (see internal region mapping sheet).
- **Allowed regions**: The set of regions in which customer content is permitted to be processed for an org/project/API key.
- **Primary region**: The default region for routing when multiple regions are allowed.
- **Region pinning**: A configuration that restricts Hosted API processing to an allowed region set.

### 3.2 Customer content (enforcement boundary)
For this policy, **customer content** includes:
- Request prompts/messages, tool/function payloads, and attachments that are provided to the model.
- Model outputs (tokens, completions, embeddings vectors derived from customer-provided input).
- Customer-provided metadata that can contain sensitive data (e.g., “user_message”, “context”, “documents”).
- Any derived artifacts that include reconstructable content (e.g., cached prefixes/KV cache entries, debug dumps).

Customer content does **not** include:
- Non-content operational metadata that does not contain sensitive data (e.g., request_id, org_id, project_id, model_id, region_id, error_code, timestamps, latency metrics).

Note: These boundaries must match ADR-021 “Region Pinning Enforcement Boundaries”. Where ambiguity exists, classify as customer content.

## 4. Policy statement (what we guarantee)
### 4.1 Hosted residency guarantee
If an organization/project/API key is configured with an allowed region set, Redwood guarantees that:
1) **Processing location**: Customer content for Hosted API requests will be processed only in the allowed region(s).
2) **No cross-region fallback with content**: Routing and fallback behavior will not send customer content to a region outside the allowed set.
3) **Deterministic enforcement**: Requests that would violate policy are blocked at request time (or at the earliest deterministic point for streaming) with a consistent error contract.
4) **Logging/telemetry boundaries**: Systems that could store customer content (including traces and debug logs) will store such content only in the allowed region(s) or will be content-redacted before leaving the region.
5) **Administrative auditability**: Changes to residency configuration are recorded in audit logs with actor, timestamp, and change details.

### 4.2 Supported residency modes
- **Single-region pin**: Allowed regions contains exactly one region (e.g., EU-only).
- **Multi-region allowed set**: Allowed regions contains multiple regions (e.g., EU + UK) with a primary.
- **No pinning**: Default routing behavior applies; residency guarantee does not apply.

### 4.3 Precedence rules (which policy applies)
Policy precedence is:
1) API key-level policy (most specific)
2) Project-level policy
3) Org-level policy (least specific)
4) No residency policy

If conflicting policies exist, the most specific applicable policy is used.

## 5. Explicit exclusions / limitations
The following are excluded from the Hosted residency guarantee unless contractually stated otherwise and implemented under separate controls:
- **Client-side routing**: If customers send requests to a region-specific endpoint that is not in their allowed set, the request will be blocked; Redwood does not control customer network paths.
- **Customer-managed storage**: Content that customers export/download/store in their own systems is outside Redwood’s residency scope.
- **Third-party processors outside region**: If a customer enables optional integrations that transmit content externally (e.g., webhooks to their own endpoints), residency depends on customer configuration.
- **Support workflows**: Support will not request raw customer prompts/outputs for troubleshooting unless explicitly approved by the customer and handled via approved secure channels; such handling is governed by Support Data Handling Policy.
- **Aggregated metrics**: Non-content operational metrics may be stored in centralized systems outside the pinned region (see Section 7.4). Metrics must not include customer content.
- **Model provider constraints**: For hosted open models running on Redwood-managed infrastructure, processing occurs in-region; if any future offering involves third-party model endpoints, it must be explicitly excluded or separately controlled and disclosed.

## 6. Control objectives
Controls must meet these objectives:
- **CO-1 (Policy correctness)**: The evaluated policy matches configured intent and is consistent across gateway and routing.
- **CO-2 (Enforcement)**: Any routing decision that would move customer content out of allowed regions is blocked.
- **CO-3 (Observability)**: Residency decisions and blocks are observable without leaking customer content.
- **CO-4 (Auditability)**: Config changes are logged and retrievable for auditors and incident response.
- **CO-5 (Operational safety)**: Enforcement failures default to a safe posture (block or in-region), with clear incident procedures.

## 7. Required engineering controls
### 7.1 Control plane: Residency Policy Service
**Requirement:** Residency policy objects must be stored and served by the control plane with authorization and validation.

Minimum requirements:
- AuthZ: Only authorized org/project admins (and internal admin roles) can create/update/delete policies.
- Validation:
  - allowed_regions must be a non-empty list when policy is enabled.
  - primary_region must be a member of allowed_regions.
  - Regions must be valid and currently supported for Hosted.
- Change control:
  - Mutations must emit an **audit log event**.
  - Policy versions must be retrievable (history) for internal investigations.

### 7.2 API Gateway: request-time validation & error contract
**Requirement:** The gateway must validate residency policy before forwarding request content to downstream systems.

- The gateway fetches or is provided residency policy context (policy_id, allowed_regions, primary_region, enforcement_mode).
- If the incoming request is targeted to or would be processed in a disallowed region, the gateway must block.
- Errors must follow the public error contract (ADR-022):
  - HTTP status code: **409 Conflict** (policy conflict) for residency violations.
  - Machine-readable error code (example): `residency_policy_violation`.
  - Response includes `request_id` and a stable `help_url`.
  - Response must not include customer content.

Streaming: If streaming starts, the system must not stream any model output if the request later evaluates as disallowed. Residency evaluation must be performed before tokens are generated.

### 7.3 Smart Routing: region selection and fallback constraints
**Requirement:** Routing decisions must treat residency as a hard constraint.

Rules:
- Candidate regions = allowed_regions (if policy exists) else default routing regions.
- Primary region is selected when healthy and capacity is available.
- Failover/fallback is permitted **only** within allowed_regions.
- Cross-region fallback outside allowed_regions is prohibited unless an explicit, customer-configured exception exists (see Section 10).

Routing must emit a structured **residency decision context** into logs/telemetry:
- request_id, org_id, project_id
- evaluated_policy_id (if any)
- allowed_regions
- selected_region
- decision_outcome: allow | block
- block_reason (if block)

### 7.4 Logging, telemetry, and tracing
**Requirement:** Customer content must not leave the allowed region via logs/traces.

Controls:
- Content redaction: Default logging configuration must redact customer content fields. Any “debug logging” that includes content must be region-scoped storage and gated behind time-limited feature flags with Security approval.
- Trace payloads: Traces may include identifiers and timing but must not include prompt text, generated text, or embedding vectors.
- Central metrics: Aggregated counters/histograms may be centrally stored cross-region if they contain no customer content (e.g., counts by error_code, latency percentiles, block rate).
- Residency decision logs: Must not include raw prompts/outputs; only structured metadata.

### 7.5 Caching and intermediate artifacts
**Requirement:** Any caching that may contain customer content (prefix/KV caches, request replay buffers) must be region-local.

- Cache keys and values must not replicate across regions.
- Cache warming strategies must not copy customer content cross-region.
- For shared multi-tenant caches, tenant isolation controls still apply; residency adds region isolation.

### 7.6 Background processing and retries
**Requirement:** Background tasks triggered by Hosted requests must execute in-region.

- Retry workers must be region-affine.
- Queueing systems must not move message payloads (containing content) outside region.
- Any exception must be treated as a residency incident.

### 7.7 Security testing and release gates
**Requirement:** Residency enforcement must be validated with automated and manual tests.

Minimum gates:
- E2E tests:
  - Pinned EU org sending traffic that would route to US must be blocked with correct error contract.
  - Streaming endpoint returns standardized residency error (not generic 5xx).
  - Cross-region fallback attempts are prevented.
- Negative testing:
  - Invalid policy configs rejected.
  - Missing/unknown region IDs handled safely (block or default-safe per design).
- Change review: Any code change that touches residency evaluation, routing, logging, or policy schema must be reviewed by Security Engineering.

### 7.8 Monitoring and alerting
**Requirement:** SRE-owned dashboards and alerts must exist for residency enforcement.

At minimum:
- Blocked requests count and rate by region, by org tier.
- Policy evaluation latency (p95/p99) to ensure enforcement does not introduce outages.
- Cross-region routing attempt counter.
- Error rate deltas after rollout by region.

Paging guidance:
- Page SRE on sustained spikes in `residency_policy_violation` that exceed baseline and correlate with customer impact.
- Page Security on any signal suggesting content may have been processed outside allowed regions.

## 8. Compliance mapping (SOC 2 / ISO 27001)
This section provides narrative mapping; exact auditor evidence is maintained in the “Data Residency Enforcement Evidence Pack v1”.

### 8.1 SOC 2 (Trust Services Criteria) mapping
- **CC6 (Logical and physical access controls)**
  - Control: AuthZ for Residency Policy Service mutations; admin RBAC; audit logs for changes.
  - Evidence: policy change audit events; access review records.
- **CC7 (System operations and change management)**
  - Control: Monitoring/alerting for blocks and anomalies; incident runbooks; release gates and testing.
  - Evidence: dashboards, alerts, incident tickets, CI results.
- **CC8 (Change management)**
  - Control: Peer review, Security review requirement, controlled rollout with feature flags.
  - Evidence: PR approvals, rollout plans, change records.
- **A1 (Availability)**
  - Control: Fail-closed behavior; in-region fallback only; capacity monitoring.
  - Evidence: routing logs showing selection within allowed regions; SLO reporting.

### 8.2 ISO/IEC 27001 mapping (illustrative)
- **A.5 / A.6 (Governance and roles)**
  - Policy ownership by Security; defined responsibilities across Platform/SRE.
- **A.8 (Asset management / information classification)**
  - Definition of customer content and handling requirements.
- **A.12 (Operations security)**
  - Monitoring, logging controls, secure operation of region-scoped systems.
- **A.14 (System acquisition, development, maintenance)**
  - SDLC gates, security review, testing.
- **A.16 (Incident management)**
  - Runbook for false positives and residency incidents; escalation paths.

## 9. Roles and responsibilities
- **Security Engineering (Marcus Lin)**: defines security requirements; reviews enforcement boundary changes; leads investigations of potential residency breaches.
- **GRC (Olga Petrov)**: maintains this policy; prepares evidence packs; supports audits and questionnaires.
- **Product (Naomi Feldman)**: owns customer-facing commitments and documentation alignment.
- **Platform Control Plane (Ethan Park)**: owns policy service implementation, validation, and migrations.
- **API Gateway (Amara Diallo / Brian Murphy)**: owns request-time enforcement and public error contract.
- **Routing (Mina Haddad / Ravi Menon)**: owns routing constraints and fallback behavior.
- **SRE (Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes)**: owns monitoring, alerts, on-call readiness, and rollback procedures.

## 10. Exceptions and emergency procedures
### 10.1 Customer exceptions
Any exception to allow cross-region processing for a pinned customer must be:
- Explicitly requested by the customer in writing, with scope and duration.
- Approved by Security Engineering and the Product owner.
- Implemented as a configuration flag with an expiry date and audit log entries.

### 10.2 Internal emergency override
Emergency override (e.g., to mitigate broad false positives) is permitted only when:
- The override does not result in processing customer content outside allowed regions.
- If the only way to restore service would violate residency, the correct action is to **block** rather than route cross-region.

All overrides must:
- Be time-bound (default max 2 hours) and logged.
- Trigger a post-incident review.

## 11. Evidence and audit readiness
Minimum evidence artifacts maintained per release:
- Policy schema and validation documentation.
- ADR-021 and ADR-022.
- Screenshots/links to dashboards and alerts.
- Sample structured residency decision logs (content-redacted).
- Audit log samples for policy create/update/delete.
- E2E test results demonstrating block behavior and non-cross-region fallback.

Retention of evidence follows Security Compliance Evidence Retention Policy.

## 12. Review cadence
- This policy must be reviewed **at least annually** or upon material changes to:
  - Regions supported for Hosted
  - Logging/tracing architecture
  - Routing/fallback design
  - Customer-facing residency commitments

Policy owner: GRC (Olga Petrov). Technical approver: CISO (Dr. Aisha Rahman).

## 13. Appendix: Standard error behavior (internal summary)
When a request is blocked due to residency:
- Status: 409
- error_code: residency_policy_violation
- message: indicates selected/target region is not in allowed set (no customer content)
- includes: request_id, help_url
- logging: decision context only; no prompt/output

For exact payload fields and SDK behavior, refer to ADR-022.

Two quick questions:\\n\\n1) If a user requests account erasure (EU), and the primary dataset is in eu-west-1 but we have geo-replicated backups in us-east-1, what acknowledgement or tombstone marker does GreenBank receive and when?\\n2) If we initiate a restore from a US replica before the EU expunge window completes, is there a risk the erased data is re-materialized?\\n\\nWe need something concise for our audit doc (one-paragraph response + any diagram). If that works I'll send a calendar invite.\\n\\nBest,\\nAditya Rao\\nDirector, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference\\naditya.rao@redwoodinference.com\\nOffice: +1 (415) 555-0123\\n\\nOn Sun, May 31, 2026 at 08:12 AM Marcus Peters <marcus.peters@greenbank.com> wrote:\\n> Hi Aditya,\\n> \\n> We are finalizing our internal compliance runbook and need to confirm exactly how Redwood surfaces deletion events for backups that cross regions....\\n\",\n    \"From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>\\nTo: Marcus Peters <marcus.peters@greenbank.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>\\nCc: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com\\nDate: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -07:00\\nSubject: Re: Quick: backup deletion acknowledgement across EU/US shards\\n\\nHi Marcus \\u2014 adding concrete details below (keeps to one paragraph then bullets for engineers):\\n\\nOne-paragraph (audit-ready): When GreenBank submits a GDPR-compliant erasure request via our API or portal, Redwood marks the primary object and all associated backup manifests with a tombstone marker and emits a DeletionEvent token (format: DE-<region>-<unix_ts>-<rand>). The DeletionEvent includes per-region targets and scheduled expunge windows; final confirmation is emitted once every replica acknowledges expunge completion. Restoration from a replica during an uncompleted expunge window is prevented by a restore-guard check which inspects DeletionEvent state and returns a non-recoverable error if the object is tagged for pending expunge. Evidence artifacts: DeletionEvent IDs, per-replica ack lines, and expunge-complete audit entries in our audit-log (audit_stream_id: as:<uuid>).\\n\\nEngineer bullets:\\n- Tombstone mechanics: primary dataset tombstone -> backup manifest tombstone -> expunge wave scheduled with priority/region ordering.\\n- Restore guard: restores check DeletionEvent state and KV tombstone version; if tombstone_version >= restore_point_version, restore is blocked.\\n- Evidence locations: audit-log (s3://redwood-audit/expunge/YYYY/MM/DD/), deletion-events index (elasticsearch://deletion-events/_doc), and per-region replication-manifest objects (bucket+manifest object keys).\\n- Timings: typical expunge wave completion for cross-region replicas: 2\\u20136 hours for same-cloud regions, up to 12\\u201318 hours for inter-cloud or high-queue conditions. Each region streams per-replica ack events into our audit-log; the DeletionEvent transitions to terminal state only once every replica reports expunge-complete.     "From: Marcus Peters <marcus.peters@greenbank.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 31 May 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick: backup deletion acknowledgement across EU/US shards

Hi Aditya,

We are finalizing our internal compliance runbook and need to confirm exactly how Redwood surfaces deletion events for backups that cross regions. Two quick questions:

1) If a user requests account erasure (EU), and the primary dataset is in eu-west-1 but we have geo-replicated backups in us-east-1, what acknowledgement or tombstone marker does GreenBank receive and when?
2) If we initiate a restore from a US replica before the EU expunge window completes, is there a risk the erased data is re-materialized?

We need something concise for our audit doc (one-paragraph response + any diagram). Can you point me to the exact evidence/logs we can reference (audit ids, timestamps)?

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Peters
Head of Platform Security | GreenBank
marcus.peters@greenbank.com

---
This message and any attachments are intended for the addressee only.",
    "From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Peters <marcus.peters@greenbank.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick: backup deletion acknowledgement across EU/US shards

Hi Marcus — thanks for the clear questions. Looping in Rishi (DR/backup lead) and Laura (Compliance) so we can give a short, audit-ready reply + a diagram.

High-level answer in one line: when an erasure request is processed the primary dataset and backup manifests are tombstoned and a coordinated expunge wave is scheduled across replicas; we emit a deletion event id that shows per-region expunge start times and final confirmation when all replicas reach expunge.

We'll follow up with:
- the minimal one-paragraph you can drop into your runbook
- a simple diagram showing tombstone propagation and the restore guardrails
- the exact log keys/audit ids you can cite.

Proposed follow-up: 30-min sync tomorrow to walk the diagram? If that works I'll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com
Office: +1 (415) 555-0123

On Sun, May 31, 2026 at 08:12 AM Marcus Peters <marcus.peters@greenbank.com> wrote:
> Hi Aditya,
> 
> We are finalizing our internal compliance runbook and need to confirm exactly how Redwood surfaces deletion events for backups that cross regions....
",
    "From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Peters <marcus.peters@greenbank.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick: backup deletion acknowledgement across EU/US shards

Hi Marcus — adding concrete details below (keeps to one paragraph then bullets for engineers):

One-paragraph (audit-ready): When GreenBank submits a GDPR-compliant erasure request via our API or portal, Redwood marks the primary object and all associated backup manifests with a tombstone marker and emits a DeletionEvent token (format: DE-<region>-<unix_ts>-<rand>). The DeletionEvent includes per-region targets and scheduled expunge windows; final confirmation is emitted once every replica acknowledges expunge completion. Restoration from a replica during an uncompleted expunge window is prevented by a restore-guard check which inspects DeletionEvent state and returns a non-recoverable error if the object is tagged for pending expunge. Evidence artifacts: DeletionEvent IDs, per-replica ack lines, and expunge-complete audit entries in our audit-log (audit_stream_id: as:<uuid>).

Engineer bullets:
- Tombstone mechanics: primary dataset tombstone -> backup manifest tombstone -> expunge wave scheduled with priority/region ordering.
- Restore guard: restores check DeletionEvent state and KV tombstone version; if tombstone_version >= restore_point_version, restore is blocked.
- Evidence locations: audit-log (s3://redwood-audit/expunge/YYYY/MM/DD/), deletion-events index (elasticsearch://deletion-events/_doc), and per-region replication-manifest objects (bucket+manifest object keys).
- Timings: typical expunge wave completion for cross-region replicas: 2–6 hours for same-cloud regions, up to 12–18 hours for inter-cloud or high-queue conditions. We include a final confirmation event when all replicas report expunge-complete.

I've attached a simplified replication diagram to illustrate the flow.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Principal SRE, DR & Backup | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: replication-diagram.png (figures showing manifest/tombstone propagation)

On Mon, Jun 1, 2026 at 10:05 AM Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Hi Marcus — thanks for the clear questions. Looping in Rishi (DR/backup lead) and Laura (Compliance) so we can give a short, audit-ready reply + a diagram....
",
    "From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Peters <marcus.peters@greenbank.com>, ops-security@greenbank.com
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2026 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick: backup deletion acknowledgement across EU/US shards — summary + artifacts

Marcus — thanks for the call yesterday. Summary and next steps below (audit-ready paragraph + artifacts you can attach to your runbook):

Audit-ready paragraph (one paragraph): When GreenBank issues an erasure request, Redwood marks objects and their backup manifests with a tombstone and emits a deletion token (DeletionEvent) that captures per-region expunge targets and scheduled windows. Each region streams per-replica ack events into our audit-log; the DeletionEvent transitions to terminal state only once every replica reports expunge-complete. During the active expunge window, our restore-guard prevents recovery from any replica that would re-materialize a tombstoned object. Evidence to cite: DeletionEvent IDs (DE-GB-1623412345-0x9f), per-replica ack lines in audit-log (s3://redwood-audit/expunge/2026/05/31/), and the replication manifest snapshot id.

Attachments and links: I've uploaded the simplified diagram and a retention matrix comparing EU/US timelines (backup-retention-matrix.pdf). Full technical appendix: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Xy_example_handshake_doc (you should have view access).

Next steps:
- I'll send the deletion-event example you can paste into your audit doc (DE-GB-1623412345-0x9f).
- Laura will follow up with our retention exception SLA language you can reference for contractual controls.
- We agreed on an evidence handoff on Fri, Jun 11 — I'll include per-replica logs and the manifest snapshot.

If you want a formal attestation PDF for your auditors, we can schedule a short addendum.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: backup-retention-matrix.pdf

Can you confirm the following for Redwood's hosted offering?\\n\\n1) Are customer request/response payloads stored at rest? If so, where (region/country) by default and can we request EU-only storage?\\n2) What are your default retention windows for request logs, embeddings, and model artifacts?\\n3) After we terminate a tenant or request erasure, what is the timeline for purging primary stores and backups?\\n4) Do backups/snapshots replicate cross-region? If so, what is the maximum retention on backups?\\n5) What controls exist for key management (KMS/HSM) and audit logs for deletion events?\\n\\nI attached our short questionnaire (crestline-sq.pdf) with the same fields. We need a short written response to include in the packet by COB Tuesday.\\n\\nThanks,\\nEmma Lopez\\nSecurity & Compliance\\nCrestline Health\\n\\nAttachment: crestline-sq.pdf (application/pdf)\",\n    \"From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>\\nTo: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>\\nCc: \\nDate: Sat, 30 May 2026 10:02:00 -07:00\\nSubject: Fwd: Hosted API - quick Q on data geography & TTL for security questionnaire\\n\\nTeam \\u2014 forwarding Crestline's three-page SQ. Can you confirm the following for Redwood's hosted offering?\\n> \\n> [snip]\",\n    \"From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>\\nTo: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>\\nDate: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 11:24:00 -07:00\\nSubject: Re: Fwd: Hosted API - quick Q on data geography & TTL for security questionnaire\\n\\nOlga \\u2014 draft answers and rationale below. I kept the language concise for inclusion in their packet; we can expand in the appendix if they want implementation details.\\n\\n1) Storage location by default- Hosted API request/response payloads and generated artifacts are persisted in the tenancy's primary region. For self\\u2011serve accounts we default to the region closest to the sign\\u2011up location (US-west for NA customers). For customers requiring EU-only storage we offer EU tenancy pinning as part of the hosted-enterprise contract (data residency addendum).\\n\\n2) Default retention windows (hosted API)\\n- Request/response logs (application payloads): default 30 days; configurable to 90/365 via contract for enterprise plans.\\n- Streaming/KV caches: ephemeral, retained only in memory and short local caches (<1 hour) unless explicitly persisted by customer choice.\\n- Embeddings & derived vectors: default 14 days; can be configured to 7 days (strict ephemeral) or retained longer if customer elects persistent vector storage under SLA.\\n- Model artifacts (snapshots, fine\\u2011tuned artifacts): retained until explicitly deleted; default snapshot retention 30 days for rolling backups.\\n\\n3) Erasure / tenant termination timelines\\n- On an account termination/erasure request we stop serving traffic immediately and mark tenant datasets for purge. Primary store purge: typical completion within 30 days.\\n- Backups / long\\u2011term snapshots: fully scrubbed within 90 days (this accounts for cross\\u2011region replication and backup windows). We provide a certificate of deletion on request after completion.\\n\\n4) Backups & cross\\u2011region replication\\n- Backups are scheduled per tenancy and may replicate to a secondary region for disaster recovery depending on the customer's SLA. For customers who require EU\\u2011only custody we ensure backups remain in\\u2011region; cross\\u2011region replication is disabled unless explicitly contracted.\\n- Maximum backup retention default is 90 days; longer retention available under contract.\\n\\n5) Key management & auditability\\n- KMS: Redwood uses cloud KMS by default for encryption at rest; enterprise customers can provide customer\\u2011managed keys (CMKs) or integrate with HSMs in private deployments.\\n- Audit logs: deletion and erasure events are logged and retained for 365 days by default in our audit trail (accessible to customers via the console for enterprise accounts).     "From: Emma Lopez <emma.lopez@crestline.health>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API - quick Q on data geography & TTL for security questionnaire

Hi Olga,

We're finalizing our vendor security questionnaire for the Crestline June board packet and have a handful of specific items on data geography, default retention, and deletion timelines for hosted APIs. Can you confirm the following for Redwood's hosted offering?

1) Are customer request/response payloads stored at rest? If so, where (region/country) by default and can we request EU-only storage?
2) What are your default retention windows for request logs, embeddings, and model artifacts?
3) After we terminate a tenant or request erasure, what is the timeline for purging primary stores and backups?
4) Do backups/snapshots replicate cross-region? If so, what is the maximum retention on backups?
5) What controls exist for key management (KMS/HSM) and audit logs for deletion events?

I attached our short questionnaire (crestline-sq.pdf) with the same fields. We need a short written response to include in the packet by COB Tuesday.

Thanks,
Emma Lopez
Security & Compliance
Crestline Health

Attachment: crestline-sq.pdf (application/pdf)",
    "From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Hosted API - quick Q on data geography & TTL for security questionnaire

Team — forwarding Crestline's three-page SQ. They need short, precise answers for their board packet (deadline Tue COB). I drafted a proposal below but want confirmation on retention numbers and the phrasing around backups + purge timelines before I send.

Main points to confirm:
- Default store region for hosted API (our standard tenancy mapping)
- Defaults for request logs vs embeddings vs model artifacts (we have flexibility for enterprise contracts)
- Wipe timeline for primary vs backups (we guarantee purge of primary within X days; full backup scrub may take longer)
- Language around KMS/HSM and customer-managed keys

I attached an internal data-residency-matrix and a suggested doc (crestline_answers_v1.docx). Please reply with any edits.

Thanks,
Olga
Head of Solutions - CSM Escalations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: crestline-sq.pdf, data-residency-matrix.xlsx, crestline_answers_v1.docx

On Sat, 30 May 2026 at 09:12, Emma Lopez <emma.lopez@crestline.health> wrote:
> Hi Olga,
> 
> We're finalizing our vendor security questionnaire for the Crestline June board packet and have a handful of specific items on data geography, default retention, and deletion timelines for hosted APIs. Can you confirm the following for Redwood's hosted offering?
> 
> [snip]",
    "From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 11:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Hosted API - quick Q on data geography & TTL for security questionnaire

Olga — draft answers and rationale below. I kept the language concise for inclusion in their packet; we can expand in the appendix if they want implementation details.

1) Storage location by default- Hosted API request/response payloads and generated artifacts are persisted in the tenancy's primary region. For self‑serve accounts we default to the region closest to the sign‑up location (US-west for NA customers). For customers requiring EU-only storage we offer EU tenancy pinning as part of the hosted-enterprise contract (data residency addendum).

2) Default retention windows (hosted API)
- Request/response logs (application payloads): default 30 days; configurable to 90/365 via contract for enterprise plans.
- Streaming/KV caches: ephemeral, retained only in memory and short local caches (<1 hour) unless explicitly persisted by customer choice.
- Embeddings & derived vectors: default 14 days; can be configured to 7 days (strict ephemeral) or retained longer if customer elects persistent vector storage under SLA.
- Model artifacts (snapshots, fine‑tuned artifacts): retained until explicitly deleted; default snapshot retention 30 days for rolling backups.

3) Erasure / tenant termination timelines
- On an account termination/erasure request we stop serving traffic immediately and mark tenant datasets for purge. Primary store purge: typical completion within 30 days.
- Backups / long‑term snapshots: fully scrubbed within 90 days (this accounts for cross‑region replication and backup windows). We provide a certificate of deletion on request after completion.

4) Backups & cross‑region replication
- Backups are scheduled per tenancy and may replicate to a secondary region for disaster recovery depending on the customer's SLA. For customers who require EU‑only custody we ensure backups remain in‑region; cross‑region replication is disabled unless explicitly contracted.
- Maximum backup retention default is 90 days; longer retention available under contract.

5) Key management & auditability
- KMS: Redwood uses cloud KMS by default for encryption at rest; enterprise customers can provide customer‑managed keys (CMKs) or integrate with HSMs in private deployments.
- Audit logs: deletion and erasure events are logged and retained for 365 days by default in our audit trail (accessible to customers via the console for enterprise accounts). Logs include the user, timestamp, object id, and operation status.

Notes on evidence: I attached the small residency matrix and architecture diagram if they want an appendix entry. Suggest we offer Crestline the EU tenancy addendum and a 30‑day primary purge / 90‑day backup scrub cadence in writing; that should be acceptable for their board.

If that reads OK, Olga, happy for you to send to Emma.

— Karthik
Director, Infrastructure Product
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-hosted-arch.pdf

On Sat, 30 May 2026 at 10:02, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Team — forwarding Crestline's three‑page SQ.
> [snip]",
    "From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Lopez <emma.lopez@crestline.health>, security@crestline.health
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API - quick Q on data geography & TTL for security questionnaire

Hi Emma — thanks for the note and the SQ. Please find our short answers below; I’ve attached a one‑page summary and the draft responses for inclusion in your packet. If your board needs tighter timelines, we can add the EU tenancy addendum and a CMK option to the order form.

Summary answers (for packet)
• Storage location: Hosted API data is persisted in the tenancy’s primary region. Self‑serve accounts default to the nearest regional cluster (US by default); EU‑only tenancy pinning is available under enterprise contract.
• Default retention: Request/response payloads are retained 30 days by default (configurable to 90/365 for enterprise). Embeddings retained 14 days by default (can be reduced to 7 days). Model snapshots retained until deleted; rolling snapshot retention default 30 days.
• Erasure timelines: Primary data purge within 30 days after a verified erasure request or tenant termination. Backups and replicated snapshots are scrubbed within 90 days; we provide a deletion attestation on completion.
• Backups & replication: Backups may replicate to a secondary region for DR depending on SLA; for EU‑only contracts cross‑region replication is disabled. Max default backup retention 90 days (extendable by agreement).
• KMS & audit: Encryption at rest via cloud KMS by default; enterprise customers may use customer‑managed keys or HSMs. Deletion/erasure events are logged in the audit trail (365‑day retention) and can be surfaced in the console or delivered as an export for enterprise customers.

Attachments: crestline_answers_v1.docx (draft answers), data-residency-matrix.xlsx, redwood-hosted-arch.pdf

Next steps: If that looks good I’ll send a formal addendum for EU tenancy pinning and CMK options. Otherwise send any edits and we’ll update the doc.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Head of Solutions - CSM Escalations
Redwood Inference

# Hosted API retention, residency, and deletion rule

Status: Support-facing corrected rule (v3)
Owner: Platform & Console
Scope: Redwood-managed Hosted API
Supersedes: v1 at this same canonical path

## What Support may state

### Retention defaults

- Customer content (prompts and outputs) is not stored persistently by default under the published Hosted retention policy.
- Debug payload logging is off unless explicitly enabled for an organization. When enabled, its default retention is 7 days.
- Operational request logs contain metadata rather than payloads and default to 14 days.
- Tracing spans linked to request IDs contain no payloads and default to 14 days.
- A verified deletion request for stored data in Redwood-managed systems completes within 30 days.

### Tenant termination and erasure

For Hosted API, an approved customer security-questionnaire response establishes the following supportable outer windows after a verified erasure request or tenant termination:

- serving is stopped and tenant datasets are marked for purge;
- primary data is purged within 30 days;
- backups and replicated snapshots are scrubbed within 90 days;
- a deletion attestation is available on completion.

These are maximum customer-facing windows. Faster internal or observed processing is not a tighter general SLA. Legal holds and separately executed contract terms can change the workflow.

### Residency

When an organization, project, or API key is configured with an allowed region set:

- customer content is processed only in the allowed region(s);
- routing does not fall back with customer content outside that set;
- a request that would violate the policy is blocked;
- logs, traces, or debug systems that could store customer content keep that content in the allowed region(s), or redact it before it leaves;
- changes to residency configuration are audited.

A single-region allowed set provides a single-region processing pin. With no pinning, the residency guarantee does not apply. Non-content operational metrics may be centralized outside the pinned region, and customer-configured third-party integrations and customer-managed storage are outside Redwood's guarantee.

## Backup and cross-region qualification

Do not claim that every Hosted backup is single-region. Approved Hosted questionnaire language says backups may replicate to a secondary region for disaster recovery depending on the customer's SLA, while EU-only contractual configurations disable cross-region replication. The Hosted residency policy does not itself create a universal backup-location promise.

When cross-region replicas exist, the documented erasure workflow tombstones the primary object and backup manifests, emits a DeletionEvent with per-region targets, blocks restore of a tombstoned object during expunge, and reaches terminal completion only after every replica acknowledges expunge. Support may use the final event and per-replica acknowledgements as case evidence, but must not promise a particular internal expunge-wave duration as a general SLA.

## Evidence and customer responses

- For routine deletion, track the verified request, primary completion, replica/backup completion, and final attestation in the support case.
- Do not apply the 10-business-day certified-decommission SLA from the Dedicated/Private playbook to Hosted API; that playbook expressly excludes Hosted.
- Do not promise raw internal logs, storage locations, or a notarized certificate. Evidence delivery must follow the approved support/security channel and customer contract.
- Check the executed order form, DPA, residency addendum, legal holds, and approved exceptions before answering.
- Any change to Redwood-managed retention requires Security and SRE review and an update to customer-facing guidance.

              "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Hosted API retention, residency, and deletion rule (v3)\nSource: agent-memory\nPath: /memory/semantic_memory/hosted-api-retention-residency-and-deletion-rule-v3-ntion_v3.md\nWorkspace: agent-memory\nTeam: Ethan Park\n\n# Hosted API retention, residency, and deletion rule (v3)\n\nMemory type: semantic_memory\nRecorded: 2026-08-04T05:14:31.273096+00:00\nConfidence: 0.96\nOwner: Ethan Park\nTags: hosted-api, retention, deletion, residency, support, v3, corrected\n\n## Summary\n\nCorrected support rule: retain the published defaults (customer content not persisted by default; opt-in debug payloads 7 days; metadata-only operational logs and no-payload traces 14 days). For verified Hosted erasure or tenant termination, use 30 days for primary purge and 90 days for backups/replicated snapshots, with an attestation on completion, subject to holds and contract terms. Configured allowed-region sets constrain customer-content processing and content-bearing logging and prevent out-of-set fallback; unpinned accounts have no residency guarantee. Backup locality is contract/SLA dependent.               "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Hosted API retention and deletion rule\nSource: Platform & Console\nPath: /knowledge/policies/hosted-api-retention.md\nWorkspace: task/ethan-park/retention-rule-v1-v3\n\n# Hosted API retention and deletion rule\n\nStatus: Support-facing interim rule (v1)\nOwner: Platform & Console\nScope: Redwood-managed Hosted API\n\n## What Support may state\n\n- Customer content (prompts and outputs) is not stored persistently by default.\n- Debug payload logging is off unless explicitly enabled for an organization. When enabled, its default retention is 7 days.\n- Operational request logs contain metadata rather than payloads and have a default retention of 14 days.\n- Tracing spans linked to request IDs contain no payloads and have a default retention of 14 days.\n- For stored data in Redwood-managed systems, Redwood completes a verified deletion request within 30 days.\n- Changes to Redwood-managed retention require Security and SRE review and an update to the customer-facing Security FAQ.\n\nThese are product defaults, not substitutes for a customer's executed contract or an approved exception.\n\n## What Support must not promise yet\n\nThe reviewed published policy does not establish:\n\n- a backup or snapshot purge deadline;\n- a tenant-termination-specific purge deadline;\n- a data-residency or single-region guarantee;\n- whether backups remain in-region or replicate cross-region;\n- a standard deletion certificate, receipt, or audit-evidence package;\n- legal-hold exceptions or treatment of billing/control-plane metadata;\n- customer-configurable Hosted API retention beyond an approved, documented exception.\n\nSales calls and questionnaire emails contain materially different figures (including 30-day payload/log retention, 72-hour primary deletion, 14- to 90-day backup purge, and region-locking statements).               "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Hosted API retention, residency, and deletion rule\nSource: Platform & Console\nPath: /knowledge/policies/hosted-api-retention.md\nWorkspace: task/ethan-park/retention-rule-correction-v3\n\n# Hosted API retention, residency, and deletion rule\n\nStatus: Support-facing corrected rule (v3)\nOwner: Platform & Console\nScope: Redwood-managed Hosted API\nSupersedes: v1 at this same canonical path\n\n## What Support may state\n\n### Retention defaults\n\n- Customer content (prompts and outputs) is not stored persistently by default under the published Hosted retention policy.\n- Debug payload logging is off unless explicitly enabled for an organization. When enabled, its default retention is 7 days.\n- Operational request logs contain metadata rather than payloads and default to 14 days.\n- Tracing spans linked to request IDs contain no payloads and default to 14 days.\n- A verified deletion request for stored data in Redwood-managed systems completes within 30 days.\n\n### Tenant termination and erasure\n\nFor Hosted API, an approved customer security-questionnaire response establishes the following supportable outer windows after a verified erasure request or tenant termination:\n\n- serving is stopped and tenant datasets are marked for purge;\n- primary data is purged within 30 days;\n- backups and replicated snapshots are scrubbed within 90 days;\n- a deletion attestation is available on completion.\n\nThese are maximum customer-facing windows. Faster internal or observed processing is not a tighter general SLA. Legal holds and separately executed contract terms can change the workflow.\n\n### Residency\n\nWhen an organization, project, or API key is configured with an allowed region set:\n\n- customer content is processed only in the allowed region(s);\n- routing does not fall back with customer content outside that set;\n- a request that would violate the policy is blocked;\n- logs, traces, or debug systems that could store customer content keep that content in the allowed region(s), or redact it before it leaves;\n- changes to residency configuration are audited.\n\nA single-region allowed set provides a single-region processing pin. With no pinning, the residency guarantee does not apply. Non-content operational metrics may be centralized outside the pinned region, and customer-configured third-party integrations and customer-managed storage are outside Redwood's guarantee.\n\n## Backup and cross-region qualification",
