            "content": "# Hosted API retention and deletion rule\n\nStatus: Support-facing interim rule (v1)\nOwner: Platform & Console\nScope: Redwood-managed Hosted API\n\n## What Support may state\n\n- Customer content (prompts and outputs) is not stored persistently by default.\n- Debug payload logging is off unless explicitly enabled for an organization. When enabled, its default retention is 7 days.\n- Operational request logs contain metadata rather than payloads and have a default retention of 14 days.\n- Tracing spans linked to request IDs contain no payloads and have a default retention of 14 days.\n- For stored data in Redwood-managed systems, Redwood completes a verified deletion request within 30 days.\n- Changes to Redwood-managed retention require Security and SRE review and an update to the customer-facing Security FAQ.\n\nThese are product defaults, not substitutes for a customer's executed contract or an approved exception.\n\n## What Support must not promise yet\n\nThe reviewed published policy does not establish:\n\n- a backup or snapshot purge deadline;\n- a tenant-termination-specific purge deadline;\n- a data-residency or single-region guarantee;\n- whether backups remain in-region or replicate cross-region;\n- a standard deletion certificate, receipt, or audit-evidence package;\n- legal-hold exceptions or treatment of billing/control-plane metadata;\n- customer-configurable Hosted API retention beyond an approved, documented exception.\n\nSales calls and questionnaire emails contain materially different figures (including 30-day payload/log retention, 72-hour primary deletion, 14- to 90-day backup purge, and region-locking statements). Do not repeat those figures as general policy until Security/SRE and Legal validate them against current production behavior and contract templates.\n\n## Validation before answering a customer\n\n1. Confirm the customer's deployment is Hosted API and identify whether debug payload logging is enabled.\n2. Check the executed order form, DPA, and approved retention/residency addenda for customer-specific terms.\n3. Escalate backup purge, termination, residency, cross-region, legal-hold, and evidence-package questions to Security/SRE and Legal.\n4. For deletion, verify the request and track completion through the support case; do not invent a backup-completion date or certificate commitment.\n5. If approved facts change, revise this canonical path and replace its semantic memory rather than publishing parallel guidance.\n\n## Evidence\n\nAuthoritative baseline:\n\n- [Customer data + logs retention policy (Hosted, Dedicated, Private)](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/customer-data-and-logs-retention-policy.json) — document `dsid_e51021765c694a65bd60b3d38b12db6e` (published Security policy).\n\nConflict/validation inputs (not authority for the unknown promises above):\n\n- [Data disposition & residency — Hosted API questionnaire](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/aditya_rao/20280220-data-disposition-hosted-api-answers-glomerate.json) — document `dsid_49ad83c4629c4d52a3873ef5c501fa5d`.\n- [Residency & evidence-gathering discovery — Silverline Capital](/knowledge/company/sources/fireflies/sales-calls/2026-06-05-residency-evidence-discovery-with-silverline-capital.json) — document `dsid_06b6ace6ae094712806536c0ccea07e0`.\n"

When enabled, its default retention is 7 days.\n- Operational request logs contain metadata rather than payloads and default to 14 days.\n- Tracing spans linked to request IDs contain no payloads and default to 14 days.\n- A verified deletion request for stored data in Redwood-managed systems completes within 30 days.\n\n### Tenant termination and erasure\n\nFor Hosted API, an approved customer security-questionnaire response establishes the following supportable outer windows after a verified erasure request or tenant termination:\n\n- serving is stopped and tenant datasets are marked for purge;\n- primary data is purged within 30 days;\n- backups and replicated snapshots are scrubbed within 90 days;\n- a deletion attestation is available on completion.\n\nThese are maximum customer-facing windows. Faster internal or observed processing is not a tighter general SLA. Legal holds and separately executed contract terms can change the workflow.\n\n### Residency\n\nWhen an organization, project, or API key is configured with an allowed region set:\n\n- customer content is processed only in the allowed region(s);\n- routing does not fall back with customer content outside that set;\n- a request that would violate the policy is blocked;\n- logs, traces, or debug systems that could store customer content keep that content in the allowed region(s), or redact it before it leaves;\n- changes to residency configuration are audited.\n\nA single-region allowed set provides a single-region processing pin. # Hosted API retention and deletion rule

Status: Support-facing interim rule (v1)
Owner: Platform & Console
Scope: Redwood-managed Hosted API

## What Support may state

- Customer content (prompts and outputs) is not stored persistently by default.
- Debug payload logging is off unless explicitly enabled for an organization. When enabled, its default retention is 7 days.
- Operational request logs contain metadata rather than payloads and have a default retention of 14 days.
- Tracing spans linked to request IDs contain no payloads and have a default retention of 14 days.
- For stored data in Redwood-managed systems, Redwood completes a verified deletion request within 30 days.
- Changes to Redwood-managed retention require Security and SRE review and an update to the customer-facing Security FAQ.

These are product defaults, not substitutes for a customer's executed contract or an approved exception.

## What Support must not promise yet

The reviewed published policy does not establish:

- a backup or snapshot purge deadline;
- a tenant-termination-specific purge deadline;
- a data-residency or single-region guarantee;
- whether backups remain in-region or replicate cross-region;
- a standard deletion certificate, receipt, or audit-evidence package;
- legal-hold exceptions or treatment of billing/control-plane metadata;
- customer-configurable Hosted API retention beyond an approved, documented exception.

Sales calls and questionnaire emails contain materially different figures (including 30-day payload/log retention, 72-hour primary deletion, 14- to 90-day backup purge, and region-locking statements). Do not repeat those figures as general policy until Security/SRE and Legal validate them against current production behavior and contract templates.

## Validation before answering a customer

# Hosted API retention, residency, and deletion rule

Status: Support-facing corrected rule (v3)
Owner: Platform & Console
Scope: Redwood-managed Hosted API
Supersedes: v1 at this same canonical path

## What Support may state

### Retention defaults

- Customer content (prompts and outputs) is not stored persistently by default under the published Hosted retention policy.
- Debug payload logging is off unless explicitly enabled for an organization. When enabled, its default retention is 7 days.
- Operational request logs contain metadata rather than payloads and default to 14 days.
- Tracing spans linked to request IDs contain no payloads and default to 14 days.
- A verified deletion request for stored data in Redwood-managed systems completes within 30 days.

### Tenant termination and erasure

For Hosted API, an approved customer security-questionnaire response establishes the following supportable outer windows after a verified erasure request or tenant termination:

- serving is stopped and tenant datasets are marked for purge;
- primary data is purged within 30 days;
- backups and replicated snapshots are scrubbed within 90 days;
- a deletion attestation is available on completion.

These are maximum customer-facing windows. Faster internal or observed processing is not a tighter general SLA. Legal holds and separately executed contract terms can change the workflow.

### Residency

When an organization, project, or API key is configured with an allowed region set:

- customer content is processed only in the allowed region(s);
- routing does not fall back with customer content outside that set;
- a request that would violate the policy is blocked;
- logs, traces, or debug systems that could store customer content keep that content in the allowed region(s), or redact it before it leaves;
- changes to residency configuration are audited.

A single-region allowed set provides a single-region processing pin. With no pinning, the residency guarantee does not apply. Non-content operational metrics may be centralized outside the pinned region, and customer-configured third-party integrations and customer-managed storage are outside Redwood's guarantee.

- Customer content (prompts and outputs) is not stored persistently by default under the published Hosted retention policy.

- Operational request logs contain metadata rather than payloads and default to 14 days.
- Tracing spans linked to request IDs contain no payloads and default to 14 days.
- A verified deletion request for stored data in Redwood-managed systems completes within 30 days.

### Tenant termination and erasure

For Hosted API, an approved customer security-questionnaire response establishes the following supportable outer windows after a verified erasure request or tenant termination:

- serving is stopped and tenant datasets are marked for purge;
- primary data is purged within 30 days;
- backups and replicated snapshots are scrubbed within 90 days;
- a deletion attestation is available on completion.

These are maximum customer-facing windows. Faster internal or observed processing is not a tighter general SLA. Legal holds and separately executed contract terms can change the workflow.

### Residency

When an organization, project, or API key is configured with an allowed region set:

- customer content is processed only in the allowed region(s);
- routing does not fall back with customer content outside that set;
- a request that would violate the policy is blocked;
- logs, traces, or debug systems that could store customer content keep that content in the allowed region(s), or redact it before it leaves;
- changes to residency configuration are audited.

A single-region allowed set provides a single-region processing pin. With no pinning, the residency guarantee does not apply. Non-content operational metrics may be centralized outside the pinned region, and customer-configured third-party integrations and customer-managed storage are outside Redwood's guarantee.

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Hosted API retention, residency, and deletion rule\nSource: Platform & Console\nPath: /knowledge/policies/hosted-api-retention.md\nWorkspace: task/ethan-park/retention-rule-correction-v3\n\n# Hosted API retention, residency, and deletion rule\n\nStatus: Support-facing corrected rule (v3)\nOwner: Platform & Console\nScope: Redwood-managed Hosted API\nSupersedes: v1 at this same canonical path\n\n## What Support may state\n\n### Retention defaults\n\n- Customer content (prompts and outputs) is not stored persistently by default under the published Hosted retention policy.\n- Debug payload logging is off unless explicitly enabled for an organization. When enabled, its default retention is 7 days.\n- Operational request logs contain metadata rather than payloads and default to 14 days.\n- Tracing spans linked to request IDs contain no payloads and default to 14 days.\n- A verified deletion request for stored data in Redwood-managed systems completes within 30 days.\n\n### Tenant termination and erasure\n\nFor Hosted API, an approved customer security-questionnaire response establishes the following supportable outer windows after a verified erasure request or tenant termination:\n\n- serving is stopped and tenant datasets are marked for purge;\n- primary data is purged within 30 days;\n- backups and replicated snapshots are scrubbed within 90 days;\n- a deletion attestation is available on completion.\n\nThese are maximum customer-facing windows. Faster internal or observed processing is not a tighter general SLA. Legal holds and separately executed contract terms can change the workflow.\n\n### Residency\n\nWhen an organization, project, or API key is configured with an allowed region set:\n\n- customer content is processed only in the allowed region(s);\n- routing does not fall back with customer content outside that set;\n- a request that would violate the policy is blocked;\n- logs, traces, or debug systems that could store customer content keep that content in the allowed region(s), or redact it before it leaves;\n- changes to residency configuration are audited.\n\nA single-region allowed set provides a single-region processing pin. With no pinning, the residency guarantee does not apply. Non-content operational metrics may be centralized outside the pinned region, and customer-configured third-party integrations and customer-managed storage are outside Redwood's guarantee.\n\n## Backup and cross-region qualification",

      "ordinal": 1,
      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Hosted API retention, residency, and deletion rule\nSource: Platform & Console\nPath: /knowledge/policies/hosted-api-retention.md\nWorkspace: task/ethan-park/retention-rule-correction-v3\n\nA single-region allowed set provides a single-region processing pin. With no pinning, the residency guarantee does not apply. Non-content operational metrics may be centralized outside the pinned region, and customer-configured third-party integrations and customer-managed storage are outside Redwood's guarantee.\n\n## Backup and cross-region qualification\n\nDo not claim that every Hosted backup is single-region. Approved Hosted questionnaire language says backups may replicate to a secondary region for disaster recovery depending on the customer's SLA, while EU-only contractual configurations disable cross-region replication. The Hosted residency policy does not itself create a universal backup-location promise.\n\nWhen cross-region replicas exist, the documented erasure workflow tombstones the primary object and backup manifests, emits a DeletionEvent with per-region targets, blocks restore of a tombstoned object during expunge, and reaches terminal completion only after every replica acknowledges expunge. Support may use the final event and per-replica acknowledgements as case evidence, but must not promise a particular internal expunge-wave duration as a general SLA.\n\n## Evidence and customer responses\n\n- For routine deletion, track the verified request, primary completion, replica/backup completion, and final attestation in the support case.\n- Do not apply the 10-business-day certified-decommission SLA from the Dedicated/Private playbook to Hosted API; that playbook expressly excludes Hosted.\n- Do not promise raw internal logs, storage locations, or a notarized certificate. Evidence delivery must follow the approved support/security channel and customer contract.\n- Check the executed order form, DPA, residency addendum, legal holds, and approved exceptions before answering.\n- Any change to Redwood-managed retention requires Security and SRE review and an update to customer-facing guidance.\n\n## Sources",

document.title: Hosted API retention, residency, and deletion rule
document.content:
# Hosted API retention, residency, and deletion rule

Status: Support-facing corrected rule (v3)
Owner: Platform & Console
Scope: Redwood-managed Hosted API
Supersedes: v1 at this same canonical path

## What Support may state

### Retention defaults

- Customer content (prompts and outputs) is not stored persistently by default under the published Hosted retention policy.
- Debug payload logging is off unless explicitly enabled for an organization. When enabled, its default retention is 7 days.
- Operational request logs contain metadata rather than payloads and default to 14 days.
- Tracing spans linked to request IDs contain no payloads and default to 14 days.
- A verified deletion request for stored data in Redwood-managed systems completes within 30 days.

### Tenant termination and erasure

For Hosted API, an approved customer security-questionnaire response establishes the following supportable outer windows after a verified erasure request or tenant termination:

- serving is stopped and tenant datasets are marked for purge;
- primary data is purged within 30 days;
- backups and replicated snapshots are scrubbed within 90 days;
- a deletion attestation is available on completion.

These are maximum customer-facing windows. Faster internal or observed processing is not a tighter general SLA. Legal holds and separately executed contract terms can change the workflow.

### Residency

When an organization, project, or API key is configured with an allowed region set:

- customer content is processed only in the allowed region(s);
- routing does not fall back with customer content outside that set;
- a request that would violate the policy is blocked;
- logs, traces, or debug systems that could store customer content keep that content in the allowed region(s), or redact it before it leaves;
- changes to residency configuration are audited.

A single-region allowed set provides a single-region processing pin. With no pinning, the residency guarantee does not apply. Non-content operational metrics may be centralized outside the pinned region, and customer-configured third-party integrations and customer-managed storage are outside Redwood's guarantee.

## Backup and cross-region qualification

Do not claim that every Hosted backup is single-region. Approved Hosted questionnaire language says backups may replicate to a secondary region for disaster recovery depending on the customer's SLA, while EU-only contractual configurations disable cross-region replication. The Hosted residency policy does not itself create a universal backup-location promise.

When cross-region replicas exist, the documented erasure workflow tombstones the primary object and backup manifests, emits a DeletionEvent with per-region targets, blocks restore of a tombstoned object during expunge, and reaches terminal completion only after every replica acknowledges expunge. Support may use the final event and per-replica acknowledgements as case evidence, but must not promise a particular internal expunge-wave duration as a general SLA.

## Evidence and customer responses

- For routine deletion, track the verified request, primary completion, replica/backup completion, and final attestation in the support case.
- Do not apply the 10-business-day certified-decommission SLA from the Dedicated/Private playbook to Hosted API; that playbook expressly excludes Hosted.
- Do not promise raw internal logs, storage locations, or a notarized certificate. Evidence delivery must follow the approved support/security channel and customer contract.
- Check the executed order form, DPA, residency addendum, legal holds, and approved exceptions before answering.
- Any change to Redwood-managed retention requires Security and SRE review and an update to customer-facing guidance.

## Sources

- [Customer data + logs retention policy (Hosted, Dedicated, Private)](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/customer-data-and-logs-retention-policy.json) — `dsid_e51021765c694a65bd60b3d38b12db6e`.
- [Hosted Data Residency Policy and Engineering Controls](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/hosted-data-residency-policy-and-controls.json) — `dsid_eb9f7314dd10443fbf70a80306d5119a`.
- [Hosted API: Data geography, TTL & purge cadence — security questionnaire response](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/aditya_rao/20260602-crestline-residency-ttl-playbook-response.json) — `dsid_7c0ce3505c1d46d8a00aa6680c35fbd3`.
- [Geo backup deletion acknowledgement and cross-region restore handshake](/knowledge/company/sources/gmail/aditya_rao/20260607-geo-backup-delete-acknowledgement-handshake.json) — `dsid_58d93b12079648b29e41e8afb78aa7cf`.
- [Tenant Decommission & Data Erasure Certification Playbook](/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process/tenant-decommission-and-data-erase-certification-playbook-2026.json) — `dsid_c7f6ff2dcf674dd784e7f65c738d0724` (scope limitation evidence).

# Hosted API retention, residency, and deletion rule (v3)

Memory type: semantic_memory
Recorded: 2026-08-04T05:14:31.273096+00:00
Confidence: 0.96
Owner: Ethan Park
Tags: hosted-api, retention, deletion, residency, support, v3, corrected

## Summary

Corrected support rule: retain the published defaults (customer content not persisted by default; opt-in debug payloads 7 days; metadata-only operational logs and no-payload traces 14 days). For verified Hosted erasure or tenant termination, use 30 days for primary purge and 90 days for backups/replicated snapshots, with an attestation on completion, subject to holds and contract terms. Configured allowed-region sets constrain customer-content processing and content-bearing logging and prevent out-of-set fallback; unpinned accounts have no residency guarantee. Backup locality is contract/SLA dependent. Cross-region erasure uses tombstones, DeletionEvent state, restore guards, and replica acknowledgements; do not promote typical internal expunge timings to a general SLA.

# Hosted API retention, residency, and deletion rule

Status: Support-facing corrected rule (v3)
Owner: Platform & Console
Scope: Redwood-managed Hosted API
Supersedes: v1 at this same canonical path

## What Support may state

### Retention defaults

- Customer content (prompts and outputs) is not stored persistently by default under the published Hosted retention policy.
- Debug payload logging is off unless explicitly enabled for an organization. When enabled, its default retention is 7 days.
- Operational request logs contain metadata rather than payloads and default to 14 days.
- Tracing spans linked to request IDs contain no payloads and default to 14 days.
- A verified deletion request for stored data in Redwood-managed systems completes within 30 days.

### Tenant termination and erasure

For Hosted API, an approved customer security-questionnaire response establishes the following supportable outer windows after a verified erasure request or tenant termination:

- serving is stopped and tenant datasets are marked for purge;
- primary data is purged within 30 days;
- backups and replicated snapshots are scrubbed within 90 days;
- a deletion attestation is available on completion.

These are maximum customer-facing windows. Faster internal or observed processing is not a tighter general SLA. Legal holds and separately executed contract terms can change the workflow.

### Residency

When an organization, project, or API key is configured with an allowed region set:

- customer content is processed only in the allowed region(s);
- routing does not fall back with customer content outside that set;
- a request that would violate the policy is blocked;
- logs, traces, or debug systems that could store customer content keep that content in the allowed region(s), or redact it before it leaves;
- changes to residency configuration are audited.

A single-region allowed set provides a single-region processing pin. With no pinning, the residency guarantee does not apply. Non-content operational metrics may be centralized outside the pinned region, and customer-configured third-party integrations and customer-managed storage are outside Redwood's guarantee.

For verified Hosted erasure or tenant termination, use 30 days for primary purge and 90 days for backups/replicated snapshots, with an attestation on completion, subject to holds and contract terms. # Hosted API retention, residency, and deletion rule

Status: Support-facing corrected rule (v3)
Owner: Platform & Console
Scope: Redwood-managed Hosted API
Supersedes: v1 at this same canonical path

## What Support may state

### Retention defaults

- Customer content (prompts and outputs) is not stored persistently by default under the published Hosted retention policy.
- Debug payload logging is off unless explicitly enabled for an organization. When enabled, its default retention is 7 days.
- Operational request logs contain metadata rather than payloads and default to 14 days.
- Tracing spans linked to request IDs contain no payloads and default to 14 days.
- A verified deletion request for stored data in Redwood-managed systems completes within 30 days.

### Tenant termination and erasure

For Hosted API, an approved customer security-questionnaire response establishes the following supportable outer windows after a verified erasure request or tenant termination:

- serving is stopped and tenant datasets are marked for purge;
- primary data is purged within 30 days;
- backups and replicated snapshots are scrubbed within 90 days;
- a deletion attestation is available on completion.

These are maximum customer-facing windows. Faster internal or observed processing is not a tighter general SLA. Legal holds and separately executed contract terms can change the workflow.

### Residency

When an organization, project, or API key is configured with an allowed region set:

- customer content is processed only in the allowed region(s);
- routing does not fall back with customer content outside that set;
- a request that would violate the policy is blocked;
- logs, traces, or debug systems that could store customer content keep that content in the allowed region(s), or redact it before it leaves;
- changes to residency configuration are audited.

A single-region allowed set provides a single-region processing pin. With no pinning, the residency guarantee does not apply. Non-content operational metrics may be centralized outside the pinned region, and customer-configured third-party integrations and customer-managed storage are outside Redwood's guarantee.

# Hosted API retention, residency, and deletion rule

Status: Support-facing corrected rule (v3)
Owner: Platform & Console
Scope: Redwood-managed Hosted API
Supersedes: v1 at this same canonical path

## What Support may state

### Retention defaults

- Customer content (prompts and outputs) is not stored persistently by default under the published Hosted retention policy.
- Debug payload logging is off unless explicitly enabled for an organization. When enabled, its default retention is 7 days.
- Operational request logs contain metadata rather than payloads and default to 14 days.
- Tracing spans linked to request IDs contain no payloads and default to 14 days.
- A verified deletion request for stored data in Redwood-managed systems completes within 30 days.

### Tenant termination and erasure

For Hosted API, an approved customer security-questionnaire response establishes the following supportable outer windows after a verified erasure request or tenant termination:

- serving is stopped and tenant datasets are marked for purge;
- primary data is purged within 30 days;
- backups and replicated snapshots are scrubbed within 90 days;
- a deletion attestation is available on completion.

These are maximum customer-facing windows. Faster internal or observed processing is not a tighter general SLA. Legal holds and separately executed contract terms can change the workflow.

### Residency

When an organization, project, or API key is configured with an allowed region set:

- customer content is processed only in the allowed region(s);
- routing does not fall back with customer content outside that set;
- a request that would violate the policy is blocked;
- logs, traces, or debug systems that could store customer content keep that content in the allowed region(s), or redact it before it leaves;
- changes to residency configuration are audited.

A single-region allowed set provides a single-region processing pin. With no pinning, the residency guarantee does not apply. Non-content operational metrics may be centralized outside the pinned region, and customer-configured third-party integrations and customer-managed storage are outside Redwood's guarantee.

A single-region allowed set provides a single-region processing pin. With no pinning, the residency guarantee does not apply. Non-content operational metrics may be centralized outside the pinned region, and customer-configured third-party integrations and customer-managed storage are outside Redwood's guarantee.

## Backup and cross-region qualification

Do not claim that every Hosted backup is single-region. Approved Hosted questionnaire language says backups may replicate to a secondary region for disaster recovery depending on the customer's SLA, while EU-only contractual configurations disable cross-region replication. The Hosted residency policy does not itself create a universal backup-location promise.

When cross-region replicas exist, the documented erasure workflow tombstones the primary object and backup manifests, emits a DeletionEvent with per-region targets, blocks restore of a tombstoned object during expunge, and reaches terminal completion only after every replica acknowledges expunge. Support may use the final event and per-replica acknowledgements as case evidence, but must not promise a particular internal expunge-wave duration as a general SLA.

## Evidence and customer responses

- For routine deletion, track the verified request, primary completion, replica/backup completion, and final attestation in the support case.
- Do not apply the 10-business-day certified-decommission SLA from the Dedicated/Private playbook to Hosted API; that playbook expressly excludes Hosted.
- Do not promise raw internal logs, storage locations, or a notarized certificate. Evidence delivery must follow the approved support/security channel and customer contract.
- Check the executed order form, DPA, residency addendum, legal holds, and approved exceptions before answering.
- Any change to Redwood-managed retention requires Security and SRE review and an update to customer-facing guidance.

Completed the two-stage Hosted API retention publication and correction. The corrected policy and memory replaced v1; no stale guidance remains visible.

### Policy revisions

- v1 — interim support rule:
  - Content not persisted by default.
  - Opt-in debug payloads: 7 days.
  - Metadata-only operational logs and no-payload traces: 14 days.
  - Verified deletion from Redwood-managed systems: within 30 days.
  - Backup purge, termination timing, residency, cross-region behavior, and deletion evidence remained explicit unknowns.

- v3 — corrected canonical rule at `/knowledge/policies/hosted-api-retention.md`:
  - Retains the v1 default-retention claims.
  - Hosted erasure/termination: primary purge within 30 days; backups and replicated snapshots within 90 days; attestation available on completion, subject to holds and contracts.
  - Configured allowed-region sets constrain customer-content processing and content-bearing logs and prevent out-of-region fallback.
  - Unpinned accounts have no residency guarantee.
  - Backup locality remains contract/SLA-dependent.
  - Replica deletion uses tombstones, DeletionEvent state, restore guards, and per-replica acknowledgements; typical internal timings are not presented as general SLAs.
  - Final document SHA-256: `549f62ef224abc6034b29dd95b2f5d6b66f739956015fafc9480faa641b054f8`.
